title: Stationary Ground-Ball Fundamentals
primarySkill: Collecting a stationary football cleanly from ground level
objective: Introduce the fundamental body position, hand shape and movement sequence required to collect a stationary football cleanly and securely.
groundSize: Pairs operate within lanes approximately five metres long and three metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 1 – Simple organisation with minimal observation or intervention
setup:
Organise players into pairs.
Place one football on the ground between each pair.
Position the collecting player two metres from the football.
The partner observes the technique and resets the football after each repetition.
Mark a finishing cone one metre beyond the football.
Players alternate after five repetitions.
Begin at walking speed.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The collecting player begins in a balanced athletic stance.
2. The player walks towards the stationary football.
3. The final steps shorten as the player approaches.
4. The knees and hips bend to lower the body.
5. The head and chest remain over the football.
6. Both hands move towards the football.
7. The player collects it cleanly with two hands.
8. The football is brought securely towards the body.
9. The player continues through the finishing cone.
10. Partners reset and change roles.
coachingPoints: Approach the football under control.
Shorten the final steps.
Lower through the knees and hips.
Keep the head and chest over the football.
Place the body behind its line.
Present both hands early.
Use the fingers rather than flat palms.
Secure the football before rising.
Continue moving after possession is established.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the approach remains controlled.
Whether the final steps shorten.
Whether the player bends through the knees.
Whether the body remains behind the football.
Whether both hands collect simultaneously.
Whether the football is secured before the player rises.
Whether balance is maintained after possession.

commonErrors.error: The player bends only from the waist.
commonErrors.correction: Lower through the knees and hips while keeping the chest strong.

commonErrors.error: The head remains behind the football.
commonErrors.correction: Move the chest and head over its line.

commonErrors.error: The player reaches with one hand.
commonErrors.correction: Present two hands and collect through the centre of the football.

commonErrors.error: The final approach is too fast.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the final steps and control momentum.

commonErrors.error: The football is lifted before it is secured.
commonErrors.correction: Wrap both hands around it before rising.

commonErrors.error: The player stops completely after collection.
commonErrors.correction: Continue through the finishing cone under control.

progressions: Move the starting cone further away.
Place the football slightly left or right.
regressions: Allow the player to start in a lowered stance.
Use a larger or softer football.
Practise the hand position without approaching.
successIndicators: Lower through the knees and hips.
Keep the body behind the football.
matchApplication: Clean ground-ball collection begins with correct body position. Players who lower effectively and place the body behind the football are more likely to maintain possession when the ball reaches ground level.
relatedDrills: HB-049 – Ground-Ball Win and Handball Exit
MK-047 – Contested Mark and Ground-Ball Recovery

title: Body-Behind-the-Football Pickup
primarySkill: Positioning the body behind the football during collection
objective: Develop the habit of placing the body directly behind the football so a missed collection is stopped by the legs or torso rather than passing into dangerous space.
groundSize: Pairs operate in lanes approximately six metres long and four metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic coaching knowledge with one main teaching point
setup:
Organise players into pairs.
Place the football at the centre of each lane.
Mark one central approach gate and two angled starting cones.
The collecting player begins from the left, right or directly in front.
The player must adjust the approach so the body finishes behind the football.
The partner resets the football.
Change roles after six repetitions.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The player begins from the nominated starting cone.
2. The collector approaches the football at controlled speed.
3. The running line is adjusted before the final two steps.
4. The player places both feet around or immediately behind the football’s line.
5. The knees and hips lower.
6. The head and chest move over the football.
7. Both hands collect and secure it.
8. The player continues through the central finishing gate.
9. The partner resets the football.
10. Repeat from all three starting angles.
coachingPoints: Adjust the running line early.
Avoid approaching from beside the football.
Place the feet around its line where possible.
Keep the chest behind and above the football.
Use the body as a safety barrier.
Present both hands.
Secure possession before moving away.
Continue through the central gate rather than drifting sideways.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the approach angle is adjusted early.
Whether the player arrives behind the football.
Whether the feet support a balanced base.
Whether the head remains over the football.
Whether a fumble would be stopped by the body.
Whether both hands secure possession.
Whether the exit remains straight and balanced.

commonErrors.error: The player approaches from the side and reaches across.
commonErrors.correction: Adjust the line earlier and move the body behind the football.

commonErrors.error: The feet remain together.
commonErrors.correction: Establish a balanced base around the ball line.

commonErrors.error: The player runs past the football.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the final steps and reduce speed.

commonErrors.error: The chest remains upright.
commonErrors.correction: Lower the hips and bring the head over the football.

commonErrors.error: The player collects outside the body line.
commonErrors.correction: Reposition the feet so the hands collect centrally.

commonErrors.error: The exit continues sideways.
commonErrors.correction: Drive through the central finishing gate after possession.

progressions: Add a passive opponent in front.
regressions: Allow the player to stop before collecting.
successIndicators: Position the body behind the football.
matchApplication: A player positioned behind the football remains competitive even when the first touch is imperfect. This is especially important in defence, wet conditions and contested situations.
relatedDrills: HB-049 – Ground-Ball Win and Handball Exit
MK-047 – Contested Mark and Ground-Ball Recovery

title: Two-Hand Clean Ground-Ball Collection
primarySkill: Securing the football cleanly with two hands at ground level
objective: Develop strong and coordinated two-hand collection so the football is secured without bouncing between the hands or being knocked forward.
groundSize: Pairs operate four to six metres apart.
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic coaching knowledge with one main teaching point
setup:
Organise players into pairs.
One player acts as the feeder.
The feeder places or rolls the football slowly towards the collector.
The collector begins two to three metres away.
Score one point only when the football is secured with one clean two-hand action.
Fumbles and body traps do not score.
Change roles after ten feeds.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The feeder places or rolls the football into the collection zone.
2. The collector approaches under control.
3. The player lowers through the knees and hips.
4. Both hands move towards the football together.
5. The fingers spread around its sides.
6. The hands close firmly at the same time.
7. The football is lifted slightly and secured against the body.
8. The player holds possession for two seconds.
9. The football is returned to the feeder.
10. Complete ten repetitions before changing roles.
coachingPoints: Keep the hands relaxed before contact.
Present both hands at the same height.
Spread the fingers around the football.
Collect through the centre rather than from one side.
Close both hands simultaneously.
Avoid slapping downward at the football.
Secure it before rising.
Hold the football firmly after collection.
Judge success by first-contact control.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether both hands arrive together.
Whether fingers wrap around the football.
Whether one hand dominates.
Whether the player pushes the football forward.
Whether possession is secured before rising.
Whether the football is trapped against the legs.
Whether first-contact control improves.

commonErrors.error: One hand reaches before the other.
commonErrors.correction: Present both hands together and close simultaneously.

commonErrors.error: The player slaps the football forward.
commonErrors.correction: Scoop around its sides rather than striking downwards.

commonErrors.error: The hands remain flat.
commonErrors.correction: Spread and curve the fingers around the football.

commonErrors.error: The player traps the football against the legs.
commonErrors.correction: Collect cleanly in front and secure with the hands.

commonErrors.error: The football spills as the player rises.
commonErrors.correction: Complete control before changing body height.

commonErrors.error: The collector looks away after first contact.
commonErrors.correction: Track the football until it is fully secured.

progressions: Vary the football slightly left and right.
regressions: Allow the player to pause before lifting.
successIndicators: Wrap the fingers around the football.
Secure it with one clean action.
matchApplication: Two-hand ground-ball collection provides the strongest first touch and prepares the football for the next disposal. Clean control becomes increasingly important under pressure and poor conditions.
relatedDrills: HB-049 – Ground-Ball Win and Handball Exit

title: Low-Body Pickup and Exit
primarySkill: Collecting the football from a low body position and exiting efficiently
objective: Develop the ability to remain low through the collection and accelerate away without standing upright too early or losing control.
groundSize: Lanes approximately eight metres long and four metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic coaching knowledge with one main teaching point
setup:
Organise players into groups of three to five.
Place the football at the centre of the lane.
Mark a starting cone three metres behind it.
Mark two exit gates, one left and one right, three metres beyond.
The coach or feeder nominates the exit side as the player approaches.
The collecting player remains low through the pickup.
Rotate after each repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The player begins at the starting cone.
2. The collector approaches the football.
3. The coach calls the left or right exit.
4. The player shortens the final steps.
5. The knees and hips lower.
6. Both hands secure the football.
7. The player remains low for the first step after collection.
8. The outside foot plants towards the nominated gate.
9. The player accelerates through the exit with the football protected.
10. The next player begins when the lane is clear.
coachingPoints: Lower before reaching the football.
Keep the head over the collection.
Secure the football with two hands.
Avoid rising vertically after possession.
Remain low through the first exit step.
Plant with balance.
Carry the football on the protected side.
Accelerate only after control is established.
Use both exit directions.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the player lowers early enough.
Whether the football is collected cleanly.
Whether the player rises too quickly.
Whether the exit step remains balanced.
Whether the correct gate is identified.
Whether the football is protected.
Whether acceleration follows control.

commonErrors.error: The player arrives upright and reaches down.
commonErrors.correction: Lower the hips during the final approach steps.

commonErrors.error: The collector stands straight up after possession.
commonErrors.correction: Stay low through the first exit step.

commonErrors.error: The football is moved to one hand too early.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain two-hand security until the direction change is complete.

commonErrors.error: The exit plant is too long and unstable.
commonErrors.correction: Use a shorter, stronger plant step.

commonErrors.error: The player exits towards the wrong gate.
commonErrors.correction: Listen for the cue while maintaining football focus.

commonErrors.error: The player accelerates before securing possession.
commonErrors.correction: Complete control before driving away.

progressions: Roll the football into the collection zone.
regressions: Allow the player to pause after collection.
successIndicators: Remain low through the first exit step.
matchApplication: Players must often collect the football and leave congestion immediately. Staying low allows quicker balance, direction change and protection from nearby opponents.
relatedDrills: HB-049 – Ground-Ball Win and Handball Exit

title: Moving Ground-Ball Pickup
primarySkill: Collecting a moving football while maintaining forward momentum
objective: Develop the ability to judge a rolling football, adjust the running line and collect cleanly without stopping before possession.
groundSize: Lanes approximately twelve metres long and five metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Organise players into groups of three to five.
Position the feeder at one end of the lane.
The collector begins eight metres away.
The feeder rolls the football into the lane at controlled speed.
Mark a finishing gate beyond the collection area.
The player must collect while moving through the lane.
Rotate feeder and collector roles regularly.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The feeder rolls the football towards the collector.
2. The player tracks its speed and line.
3. The collector approaches at controlled pace.
4. The final steps shorten as the football nears.
5. The running line adjusts behind the football.
6. The player lowers through the knees and hips.
7. Both hands collect the football cleanly.
8. The player remains moving through possession.
9. The football is carried through the finishing gate.
10. Players rotate roles.
coachingPoints: Track the football from the feeder’s release.
Judge both speed and direction.
Avoid sprinting beyond the collection point.
Adjust the running line early.
Shorten the final steps.
Lower without stopping.
Collect with two hands.
Continue moving through the pickup.
Secure possession before increasing speed.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the player judges the roll.
Whether the approach speed is appropriate.
Whether the running line finishes behind the football.
Whether the body lowers while moving.
Whether both hands collect cleanly.
Whether the player stops before possession.
Whether balance is maintained through the gate.

commonErrors.error: The player sprints past the football.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce speed earlier and shorten the final steps.

commonErrors.error: The collector approaches from beside the line.
commonErrors.correction: Adjust early and place the body behind the roll.

commonErrors.error: The player stops before collecting.
commonErrors.correction: Lower while continuing forward through the ball.

commonErrors.error: The hands reach before the body is positioned.
commonErrors.correction: Move the feet first, then collect centrally.

commonErrors.error: The football rebounds from rigid hands.
commonErrors.correction: Relax before contact and wrap the fingers around it.

commonErrors.error: The player increases speed before possession is secure.
commonErrors.correction: Confirm control before accelerating.

progressions: Vary the roll left and right.
regressions: Allow the collector to begin closer.
matchApplication: Most ground balls continue moving after a spoil, poor kick or deflection. Players must adjust their feet and speed rather than treating every pickup as stationary.
relatedDrills: HB-049 – Ground-Ball Win and Handball Exit
MK-047 – Contested Mark and Ground-Ball Recovery

title: Left-and-Right Ground-Ball Collection
primarySkill: Collecting footballs arriving to either side of the body
objective: Develop the ability to move laterally, place the body behind a football arriving off line and collect cleanly on both sides.
groundSize: Lanes approximately ten metres long and eight metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Position the feeder at one end of the lane.
The collector begins six to eight metres away.
Mark collection gates two metres left and right of the centre line.
The feeder rolls the football towards either gate.
The collector must adjust laterally and place the body behind the football.
A third player waits for rotation.
Complete equal repetitions to both sides.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The feeder rolls the football towards the left or right collection gate.
2. The collector identifies the direction.
3. The player uses lateral adjustment steps.
4. The running line curves behind the football.
5. The final steps shorten.
6. The body lowers and squares to the football.
7. Both hands collect it cleanly.
8. The player exits forward through the same gate.
9. Roles rotate after each repetition.
10. Complete equal left- and right-side attempts.
coachingPoints: React to the roll rather than guessing.
Move the feet before reaching with the hands.
Use lateral steps before turning the body forward.
Curve behind the football’s line.
Avoid collecting across the body.
Present both hands.
Remain balanced on both sides.
Continue forward after possession.
Practise the less comfortable side equally.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the player reacts to the actual roll.
Whether lateral movement begins quickly.
Whether the body reaches the football’s line.
Whether the collector reaches across the body.
Whether both hands are used.
Whether one side is less controlled.
Whether the player exits in balance.

commonErrors.error: The player reaches across without moving the feet.
commonErrors.correction: Adjust laterally and place the body behind the football.

commonErrors.error: The collector approaches from the inside side of the roll.
commonErrors.correction: Curve around and collect through its centre line.

commonErrors.error: The outside foot crosses awkwardly and causes imbalance.
commonErrors.correction: Use short lateral steps before turning forward.

commonErrors.error: One hand collects while the other remains behind.
commonErrors.correction: Present both hands together.

commonErrors.error: The player avoids the non-preferred side.
commonErrors.correction: Alternate every repetition and maintain equal volume.

commonErrors.error: The exit drifts across the lane.
commonErrors.correction: Continue forward through the collection gate.

progressions: Add an immediate disposal to the opposite side.
regressions: Allow the player to begin closer.
Use one side at a time.
successIndicators: Position the body behind the football.
matchApplication: Ground balls rarely arrive directly in front. Players must move laterally and reposition the body rather than reaching across and exposing the football.

title: Ground-Ball Approach Footwork
primarySkill: Using controlled approach and adjustment footwork before collection
objective: Develop the footwork required to reach the football’s line, control momentum and establish a balanced collection position.
groundSize: Lanes approximately twelve metres long and six metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Mark an approach lane with three adjustment cones before the collection zone.
Position the feeder at the far end.
The collector begins eight to ten metres away.
The feeder may roll the football short, central or slightly wide.
The player must use the adjustment area to control speed and line.
The cones guide shorter final steps without creating a rigid running pattern.
Rotate roles after each repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The feeder rolls the football into the collection zone.
2. The player accelerates through the first section.
3. The collector reads the football’s speed and line.
4. The player enters the adjustment area.
5. Stride length reduces progressively.
6. The feet reposition behind the football.
7. The body lowers into the collection.
8. Both hands secure possession.
9. The player exits through the finishing gate.
10. Roles rotate and the roll type changes.
coachingPoints: Use early speed to reach the contest.
Decelerate before the final collection point.
Avoid one large braking step.
Use several shorter adjustment steps.
Reposition the feet behind the football.
Lower while maintaining balance.
Keep the hands free until the body is positioned.
Secure possession before accelerating.
Adapt the footwork to each roll.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the player accelerates initially.
Whether deceleration begins early enough.
Whether the final steps shorten.
Whether one large step creates imbalance.
Whether the feet reach the football’s line.
Whether the body lowers under control.
Whether possession is secured before exit.

commonErrors.error: The player approaches at one speed.
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate early and reduce stride length near the football.

commonErrors.error: The collector uses one large stopping step.
commonErrors.correction: Use several shorter adjustment steps.

commonErrors.error: The feet stop beside the football.
commonErrors.correction: Reposition behind the line before collecting.

commonErrors.error: The player reaches while still running too fast.
commonErrors.correction: Control momentum before the hands engage.

commonErrors.error: The head lifts before possession is secure.
commonErrors.correction: Track the football through the complete collection.

commonErrors.error: The player remains slow after collecting.
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate once control and balance are established.

matchApplication: Efficient ground-ball players arrive quickly but do not overrun the football. Controlled final footwork allows clean hands and a faster next action.
relatedDrills: MK-005 – Marking Footwork to the Football Line

title: Pickup, Protect and Handball
primarySkill: Collecting a ground ball, protecting possession and releasing by handball
objective: Develop the complete sequence of collecting the football, protecting it from pressure and releasing a supporting teammate with an accurate handball.
groundSize: Corridors approximately twelve metres long and eight metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Position the football in the centre of the corridor.
Player A begins behind the football.
Players B and C begin in left and right support positions.
Player D waits as the feeder or rotation player.
The coach nominates or signals which support player becomes active.
Player A collects, protects and handballs to the active support runner.
Players rotate through all roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Player A approaches the football.
2. Players B and C begin controlled support movement.
3. Player A lowers and collects with two hands.
4. The football is secured against the body.
5. The coach identifies the active support side.
6. Player A turns the body to protect the football from the opposite side.
7. The football is placed on the supporting hand.
8. Player A handballs into the receiver’s forward path.
9. The receiver collects and exits through the finishing gate.
10. Players rotate roles.
coachingPoints: Complete the ground-ball collection before preparing the handball.
Use two hands through first contact.
Keep the body between imagined pressure and the football.
Lift the eyes after possession is secured.
Select the correct supporting hand.
Use a legal fist strike.
Lead the receiver forward.
Avoid standing upright before disposal.
Maintain balance through the handball action.
Support players should communicate.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the football is collected cleanly.
Whether Player A protects possession.
Whether scanning occurs after control.
Whether the active support side is recognised.
Whether the handball technique remains legal.
Whether the receiver is led forward.
Whether the player stays balanced and low.

commonErrors.error: The player prepares the handball before securing the pickup.
commonErrors.correction: Complete two-hand control first.

commonErrors.error: The football is exposed to the imagined pressure side.
commonErrors.correction: Turn the body and protect it on the opposite hip.

commonErrors.error: The player looks for support before collecting.
commonErrors.correction: Track the football first, then lift the eyes.

commonErrors.error: The handball platform is unstable.
commonErrors.correction: Hold the football firmly on the supporting hand.

commonErrors.error: The handball travels behind the receiver.
commonErrors.correction: Release earlier into the forward running path.

commonErrors.error: The player stands upright and loses balance.
commonErrors.correction: Remain low through collection and release.

progressions: Allow the collector to choose the support side.
regressions: Allow the collector to stop before handballing.
matchApplication: Winning a ground ball is only the first part of the possession. Players must protect it and release support accurately before pressure closes.
relatedDrills: HB-049 – Ground-Ball Win and Handball Exit

title: Pickup, Balance and Kick
primarySkill: Collecting a ground ball and preparing an accurate kick
objective: Develop the ability to collect the football cleanly, regain balance and complete an accurate kick without rushing the transition from ground level.
groundSize: Lanes approximately fifteen to twenty metres long and six metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Position the football six to eight metres from the starting cone.
Mark a target gate ten to fifteen metres beyond the collection point.
Player A begins as the collector.
Player B waits inside the target gate.
Player C resets the football.
Player D waits for rotation.
The collector must secure, balance and kick accurately.
Rotate after every repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Player A approaches the football.
2. The player lowers and collects with two hands.
3. The football is secured against the body.
4. Player A rises into a balanced running position.
5. The eyes lift towards Player B.
6. The football is organised for the chosen kicking foot.
7. The player shortens the final step.
8. An accurate kick is delivered through the target gate.
9. Player B marks and carries the football to the reset position.
10. Players rotate roles.
coachingPoints: Complete the pickup before organising the kick.
Maintain two-hand control while rising.
Lift the eyes after possession is secure.
Avoid kicking from the first unstable step.
Establish balance and alignment.
Organise the football cleanly onto the kicking side.
Use an appropriate kick for the distance.
Deliver to the receiver’s advantage.
Continue supporting after disposal.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the ground ball is collected cleanly.
Whether the player rushes the kick.
Whether balance is established.
Whether the football is organised efficiently.
Whether the player scans the target.
Whether the kick is accurate.
Whether the receiver can mark without excessive adjustment.

commonErrors.error: The player begins kicking before securing the pickup.
commonErrors.correction: Complete possession first.

commonErrors.error: The football moves to one hand too early.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain two-hand control until balance is established.

commonErrors.error: The player kicks from an unstable first step.
commonErrors.correction: Take an additional controlled step before disposal.

commonErrors.error: The eyes remain down after collection.
commonErrors.correction: Lift the head once the football is secure.

commonErrors.error: The ball drop becomes rushed.
commonErrors.correction: Organise the football calmly onto the kicking side.

commonErrors.error: The kick misses the target gate.
commonErrors.correction: Align the body and use the appropriate force for the distance.

progressions: Roll the football into the collection.
regressions: Allow the collector to stop before kicking.
matchApplication: Players frequently collect loose footballs before kicking. Rushing directly from a low pickup into disposal often causes poor balance, ball drop and accuracy.

title: Ground-Ball Fundamentals Assessment
primarySkill: Assessing fundamental ground-ball collection and post-possession execution
objective: Assess whether players can approach, collect, secure and use a ground ball through fundamental stationary, moving and disposal-based tasks.
groundSize: Five assessment stations arranged within an area approximately thirty-five metres × twenty-five metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Establish five assessment stations:
Station 1: Stationary two-hand collection.
Station 2: Body-behind-the-football collection from varied angles.
Station 3: Moving and left-right rolling footballs.
Station 4: Pickup, protect and handball.
Station 5: Pickup, balance and kick.
Divide players evenly between stations.
Assign a coach or trained observer where possible.
Standardise roll speed and disposal distance.
Allow one practice repetition before formal scoring.
Record technical collection and post-possession execution separately.
Repeat clearly unsuitable feeds.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. At Station 1, each player completes eight stationary collections.
2. At Station 2, each player completes two collections from the front, left and right.
3. At Station 3, each player completes six moving-football pickups with varied direction.
4. At Station 4, each player completes four pickup-and-handball sequences.
5. At Station 5, each player completes four pickup-and-kick sequences.
6. Observers assess approach, footwork, body position, hand control and security.
7. Post-collection balance, scanning and disposal accuracy are also recorded.
8. Players rotate after all group members complete the station.
9. Each player receives one strength and one priority correction.
10. Players repeat the station linked to their lowest score.
coachingPoints: Apply consistent standards across all stations.
Assess the approach before the hands reach the football.
Record whether the body finishes behind the ball line.
Observe knee and hip flexion.
Judge the collection by first-contact control.
Assess whether both hands work together.
Include security while the player rises.
Record whether the next disposal begins only after possession is established.
Separate poor feeds from player error.
Feedback should identify one clear technical action.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players control approach speed.
Whether final steps shorten.
Whether the body reaches the football’s line.
Whether players lower through the knees and hips.
Whether the football is secured with two hands.
Whether players maintain possession while rising.
Whether left-and-right collections remain balanced.
Whether handballs and kicks follow clean control.
Whether feedback is applied during reassessment.

commonErrors.error: The player approaches too quickly and overruns the football.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce stride length during the final steps.

commonErrors.error: The collector reaches from beside the football.
commonErrors.correction: Adjust the feet and place the body behind its line.

commonErrors.error: The player bends only from the waist.
commonErrors.correction: Lower through the knees and hips.

commonErrors.error: One hand dominates the collection.
commonErrors.correction: Present both hands together and close simultaneously.

commonErrors.error: The football spills as the player rises.
commonErrors.correction: Secure it fully before changing body height.

commonErrors.error: The player stops before every moving pickup.
commonErrors.correction: Collect while continuing forward under control.

commonErrors.error: The handball or kick begins before possession is secure.
commonErrors.correction: Complete the pickup, regain balance and then dispose.

commonErrors.error: Assessment scores are affected by poor feeds.
commonErrors.correction: Repeat unsuitable rolls and standardise delivery quality.

progressions: Repeat the assessment later in the training phase.
successIndicators: Position the body behind the football.
matchApplication: Fundamental ground-ball performance combines approach, body positioning, clean hands and the ability to complete the next action. This assessment confirms whether players can control possession before pressure is introduced.

title: Unpredictable Bounce Ground-Ball Collection
primarySkill: Adjusting body position and hand placement to collect an unpredictably bouncing football
objective: Develop the ability to read an irregularly bouncing football, adjust the feet and body late, and secure possession without reaching, snatching or overrunning the collection point.
groundSize: Lanes approximately twelve metres long and six metres wide.
equipment: Optional uneven bounce mats or low-profile training pads
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Organise players into groups of three to five.
Create a twelve-metre lane with a feeder positioned at one end.
Mark a collection area approximately four metres long in the middle of the lane.
Position the collector six to eight metres from the collection area.
Place a finishing gate three metres beyond the collection area.
The feeder delivers bouncing footballs using different release angles, speeds and bounce points.
All feeds must remain safe and collectable.
Where bounce mats are used, position them securely so they cannot move or create a tripping hazard.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder releases a football so it bounces unpredictably within the collection area.
The collector tracks the football from the feeder’s release.
The collector approaches under control rather than committing to the first expected bounce line.
As the football changes height or direction, the player adjusts with short, active steps.
The player positions the body as close as possible behind the football’s final line.
The hands remain low, relaxed and ready to move with the bounce.
The collector secures the football with two hands against the body.
The player maintains balance and carries the football through the finishing gate.
The collector returns outside the lane while the next player begins.
Players rotate through the feeder role after four to six repetitions.
coachingPoints: Track the football continuously rather than watching the ground in front of it.
Maintain a controlled approach that allows a late adjustment.
Use short steps as the football enters the collection area.
Keep the hips, knees and ankles flexed so the hands can change height quickly.
Move the feet before reaching sideways with the hands.
Present soft hands that travel with the football on contact.
Secure the football before accelerating out of the collection.
Where the bounce rises sharply, absorb it into the hands and body rather than attempting to slap it down.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the player watches the football from release to collection.
Whether approach speed allows a late change of direction.
Whether the feet remain active after an unexpected bounce.
Whether the body reaches the football’s line.
Whether the hands adjust to the football’s height.
Whether the player reaches from a rigid or upright position.
Whether possession is secured cleanly against the body.
Whether the player exits under control after collection.

commonErrors.error: The player predicts the bounce too early and runs past the football.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce approach speed and remain square until the bounce becomes clear.

commonErrors.error: The collector stops the feet and reaches sideways.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the feet active and move the body back onto the football’s line.

commonErrors.error: The player stands upright as the football rises.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain knee and hip flexion so the hands can adjust without losing balance.

commonErrors.error: The hands are rigid and the football rebounds away.
commonErrors.correction: Relax the fingers and absorb the football into the hands and body.

commonErrors.error: The player slaps downward at a high bounce.
commonErrors.correction: Receive the football at its available height and bring it securely to the body.

commonErrors.error: The collector accelerates before establishing possession.
commonErrors.correction: Confirm two-hand control before increasing running speed.

progressions: Increase the speed and variation of the feed.
Deliver footballs that bounce to either side of the collector.
Require an immediate handball or kick after collection.
Introduce wet footballs where ground conditions remain safe.
regressions: Deliver the football directly towards the collector.
Allow the player to begin inside the collection area.
Remove bounce mats and use controlled hand bounces.
Return temporarily to a rolling football.
successIndicators: Track the complete flight and bounce of the football.
Adjust their feet after an irregular bounce.
Maintain a low and balanced body position.
Complete the drill without overrunning the football.
matchApplication: Spoils, deflections, wet conditions and pressured disposals regularly create unpredictable bounces. Players who remain balanced and adjustable are more likely to secure possession rather than committing early and allowing the football to pass beneath or beside them.

title: Half-Volley Gather Fundamentals
primarySkill: Gathering a football immediately after it contacts the ground
objective: Teach players to gather a football cleanly on the first rise after the bounce by matching the hands to the football’s movement and maintaining the body behind the collection.
groundSize: Lanes approximately eight metres long and four metres wide.
equipment: Flat markers indicating the bounce zone
Optional junior-sized footballs for younger players
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Organise players into pairs or groups of three.
Position the feeder at one end of an eight-metre lane.
Mark a bounce zone approximately one to two metres in front of the collector.
The collector begins three to four metres from the bounce zone.
Place a finishing gate two metres behind the collection point.
The feeder delivers a controlled downward bounce that reaches the collector on its first rise.
Begin with slow, consistent feeds before introducing variation.
Rotate the feeder after five repetitions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The collector begins in an athletic stance and watches the feeder’s release.
The feeder bounces the football into the marked zone.
The collector moves forward and adjusts the feet to remain behind the football.
The player lowers through the knees and hips before the football reaches the ground.
As the football rises, the hands move forward and down to meet it early.
The fingers remain open, relaxed and directed around the football.
The player cushions the football into two-hand control rather than striking at it.
Possession is brought securely towards the body.
The collector rises in balance and moves through the finishing gate.
Players reset and repeat before rotating roles.
coachingPoints: Read the feeder’s release and identify the likely bounce point.
Reach the bounce line with the body, not only the hands.
Lower before the football rises.
Keep the head steady and the eyes focused on the lower half of the football.
Meet the football early on its first rise.
Place the hands behind and slightly around the football’s movement.
Cushion the football rather than attempting to trap it rigidly.
Secure possession before standing or preparing the next disposal.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the player identifies the bounce point early.
Whether the body arrives behind the football.
Whether the player lowers before the football rises.
Whether the hands meet the football rather than waiting at the body.
Whether the fingers remain relaxed and open.
Whether the football is cushioned into possession.
Whether the player maintains balance while rising.
Whether the collector remains confident after an unsuccessful attempt.

commonErrors.error: The player waits upright for the football to rise.
commonErrors.correction: Lower before the bounce and take the football closer to ground level.

commonErrors.error: The collector reaches with straight, rigid arms.
commonErrors.correction: Soften the elbows and allow the hands to travel with the football.

commonErrors.error: The player places the hands above the football.
commonErrors.correction: Position the hands behind and around its rising line.

commonErrors.error: The body remains beside the bounce line.
commonErrors.correction: Adjust the feet so the chest finishes behind the football.

commonErrors.error: The player attempts to pin the football against the ground.
commonErrors.correction: Meet it on the rise and cushion it into the hands.

commonErrors.error: The player looks away before possession is complete.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain vision on the football until it is secured.

progressions: Vary the height and speed of the bounce.
Bounce the football slightly left or right.
Require the collector to continue running through the gather.
Add an immediate handball to the feeder.
Reduce the size of the bounce zone.
regressions: Use a larger and slower bounce.
Allow the player to begin closer to the bounce point.
Permit the player to start in a lowered stance.
Use a stationary football to rehearse hand shape.
Allow the football to bounce twice before collection.
Use a softer junior football for introductory groups.
successIndicators: Position the body behind the football.
Meet the football early with both hands.
Move smoothly into the next action.
matchApplication: A low kick, deflection or awkward handball may reach a player immediately after bouncing. Gathering the football on the half-volley prevents it rising into the body, passing underneath the hands or creating an opportunity for an opponent to contest possession.

title: Front-and-Centre Crumb Collection
primarySkill: Positioning and moving front-and-centre to collect a spilled football
objective: Develop the ability to establish an effective front-and-centre position, read a football spilling from a marking contest and collect it while maintaining forward movement.
groundSize: Channels approximately fifteen metres long and eight metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Organise players into groups of four to six.
Position a feeder at one end of the channel.
Place a designated contest player or marking bag approximately eight metres away.
Mark a front-and-centre starting arc two to four metres in front of the contest.
The crumber begins outside the immediate drop zone and moves onto the arc as the feed is delivered.
The contest player deliberately directs or spills the football into one of three marked crumb zones.
Place two exit gates at forty-five-degree angles beyond the collection area.
Rotate players through feeder, contest and crumbing roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder delivers the football towards the contest player or marking bag.
The crumber begins moving towards a front-and-centre position.
The contest player taps or spills the football into one of the marked crumb zones.
The crumber reads the direction of the spill while remaining on the move.
The player adjusts the running line and approaches the football under control.
The body lowers and finishes behind the football’s path.
The crumber collects with two hands.
The player exits through the gate that provides the clearest forward route.
The football is returned to the feeder.
Players rotate roles after three to four repetitions.
coachingPoints: Begin outside the immediate feet of the contest so there is room to react.
Arrive front-and-centre as the football reaches the contest.
Maintain movement rather than standing beneath the contest.
Watch the football through the hands of the contest player.
Read the spill before accelerating fully.
Adjust the feet to collect from behind the football.
Keep the body low through possession.
Exit at an angle that avoids returning directly into the contest.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the crumber begins at an appropriate distance from the contest.
Whether the player arrives at the correct time.
Whether the player remains moving as the football spills.
Whether the eyes stay on the football through the contest.
Whether the running line adjusts to the spill.
Whether the body finishes behind the football.
Whether collection is clean and secure.
Whether the exit moves away from the original contest.

commonErrors.error: The crumber stands directly underneath the contest.
commonErrors.correction: Begin two to four metres away and arrive as the football spills.

commonErrors.error: The player waits flat-footed for the outcome.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain light movement and prepare to react in either direction.

commonErrors.error: The crumber moves behind rather than front-and-centre.
commonErrors.correction: Reposition towards the likely forward spill zone.

commonErrors.error: The player watches the contest player instead of the football.
commonErrors.correction: Track the football through the hands and into the spill.

commonErrors.error: The collector attacks at full speed and overruns the crumb.
commonErrors.correction: Control the final steps before lowering into the pickup.

commonErrors.error: The exit returns the player into congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Use the angled gate that moves away from the contest.

progressions: Allow the contest player to direct the spill to any location.
Add a second crumber competing for position without contact.
Add a passive defender near one exit gate.
Require an immediate handball or kick.
Increase the speed and height of the initial feed.
Begin from a wider forward or midfield starting position.
regressions: Use a stationary coach-held football that is dropped into the collection area.
Reduce the distance between the crumber and the contest.
successIndicators: Time their arrival with the contest.
Track the football through the spill.
matchApplication: Front-and-centre positioning allows forwards, midfielders and defenders to win possession when a mark is not completed. Correct positioning gives the crumber a forward-facing collection opportunity and reduces the likelihood of the football passing through the contest uncontested.
relatedDrills: HB-049 – Ground-Ball Win and Handball Exit
MK-047 – Contested Mark and Ground-Ball Recovery

title: Chasing Ground-Ball Collection
primarySkill: Collecting a football travelling away in the same direction as the player
objective: Develop the ability to chase down a football travelling away, match its speed and collect it cleanly without overrunning, toe-poking or losing forward momentum.
groundSize: Lanes approximately eighteen metres long and five metres wide.
equipment: Bibs where multiple groups share an area
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Create lanes eighteen metres long and five metres wide.
Position a feeder two metres behind the collector’s starting marker.
Mark a collection gate ten to twelve metres down the lane.
Place a finishing gate three metres beyond the collection gate.
The feeder rolls the football past the collector so it travels away down the lane.
Organise groups of three to five players.
Ensure adjacent lanes are separated sufficiently for safe running.
Rotate the feeder after four repetitions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The collector begins facing down the lane.
The feeder rolls the football past the player at controlled speed.
The collector reacts and accelerates after the football.
The player judges its speed and running line.
As the player closes the distance, running speed is matched to the football.
The final steps shorten without stopping.
The player lowers while continuing forward.
Both hands gather the football from behind its line.
The collector secures possession and runs through the finishing gate.
The next player begins once the lane is clear.
coachingPoints: Accelerate early enough to reach the football without panicking at the collection point.
Track the football over the final metres rather than looking only downfield.
Match the football’s speed before lowering the hands.
Shorten the final steps to prevent overrunning.
Lower the body while continuing to run.
Approach directly from behind whenever possible.
Scoop the football into two-hand control without pushing it farther forward.
Secure possession before returning to full acceleration.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the player reacts promptly to the roll.
Whether acceleration is controlled.
Whether the player reaches the football from behind.
Whether running speed is reduced appropriately before collection.
Whether the player stays low while moving.
Whether both hands gather beneath and around the football.
Whether the collector avoids kicking or pushing the football ahead.
Whether forward momentum continues after possession.

commonErrors.error: The player reaches the football at excessive speed.
commonErrors.correction: Begin speed matching earlier and shorten the final steps.

commonErrors.error: The collector bends only from the waist.
commonErrors.correction: Lower through the knees and hips while maintaining running balance.

commonErrors.error: The player runs beside the football and reaches across.
commonErrors.correction: Adjust the running line and collect directly from behind.

commonErrors.error: The football is pushed farther forward by rigid hands.
commonErrors.correction: Present soft hands underneath and around the football.

commonErrors.error: The player toe-pokes the football unnecessarily.
commonErrors.correction: Close under control and use the hands when clean possession is available.

commonErrors.error: The collector stops after gathering.
commonErrors.correction: Carry momentum through the football and into the finishing gate.

progressions: Increase the speed of the roll.
Roll the football on a slight diagonal.
Add an immediate disposal after collection.
Require collection and exit through a nominated side gate.
regressions: Allow the collector to start closer to the football.
Place the football stationary within the collection gate.
Rehearse the final three collection steps without a chase.
successIndicators: Judge the speed of the football.
Maintain possession and momentum through the exit.
matchApplication: Players frequently chase footballs rolling towards goal, the boundary or open space. Matching speed before collection allows the player to gain possession cleanly while remaining capable of accelerating into the next phase.

title: Boundary-Line Ground-Ball Recovery
primarySkill: Collecting a ground ball near the boundary while maintaining possession and field position
objective: Teach players to approach and collect a football near the boundary with the body positioned between the football and the line, then exit safely back into the field of play.
groundSize: Channels approximately fifteen metres long and seven metres wide, positioned alongside a marked boundary line.
equipment: Boundary cones or existing boundary line
Optional boundary throw-in bag for visual reference
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Mark a straight boundary line using cones where an existing line is unavailable.
Create a fifteen-metre channel extending parallel to the boundary.
Position the feeder at one end of the channel.
The collector begins five to seven metres infield from the football’s expected path.
Mark two inboard exit gates at forty-five-degree angles from the collection point.
The feeder rolls the football so it travels within one metre of the boundary.
Players rotate through feeder and collector roles.
Ensure the exercise is conducted away from fences, benches and other obstacles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder rolls the football towards the boundary-side collection area.
The collector approaches from an infield starting position.
The player curves the running line to reach the boundary side of the football where possible.
The body is positioned between the football and the boundary line.
The player controls speed and lowers through the collection.
Both hands secure the football before it crosses the line.
The collector turns or arcs back inboard.
The player exits through one of the two inboard gates.
A successful repetition requires clean possession without stepping over the boundary.
Players reset and rotate roles after four repetitions.
coachingPoints: Recognise the boundary before reaching the football.
Use an approach angle that places the body between the football and the line.
Avoid running directly at the boundary with no exit route.
Shorten the final steps and lower under control.
Keep both hands low and inside the field of play.
Secure the football before changing direction.
Use the outside shoulder and hip to protect the boundary side.
Exit inboard rather than continuing along or over the line.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the player identifies the boundary early.
Whether the approach creates a safe collection angle.
Whether the body reaches the boundary side of the football.
Whether the player remains balanced near the line.
Whether the football is collected before crossing the boundary.
Whether possession is secure before the turn.
Whether the exit returns the player inboard.
Whether players avoid unnecessary diving or sliding.

commonErrors.error: The player approaches directly from infield and allows the football to cross the line.
commonErrors.correction: Curve the approach and reach the boundary side before collecting.

commonErrors.error: The collector runs parallel to the boundary with no inboard exit.
commonErrors.correction: Approach on an angle that opens the body towards the field.

commonErrors.error: The player steps over the line while gathering.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce speed earlier and shorten the final steps.

commonErrors.error: The football is collected with one extended hand.
commonErrors.correction: Lower the body and present two hands inside the field of play.

commonErrors.error: The player turns before possession is secure.
commonErrors.correction: Complete the collection before rotating the hips and shoulders.

commonErrors.error: The collector dives unnecessarily near the line.
commonErrors.correction: Stay on the feet and use controlled approach speed whenever possible.

progressions: Vary whether the football remains in play or moves towards the line.
Add a passive opponent approaching from infield.
Reduce the width of the inboard exit gates.
Begin the collector from behind the football.
regressions: Place the football stationary near the boundary.
Increase the distance between the football and the line.
Allow the player to walk through the positioning pattern.
successIndicators: Place the body between the football and the line.
Secure the football with two hands.
matchApplication: Boundary ground balls require players to protect possession while accounting for the line and the reduced space available. Reaching the boundary side of the football preserves the chance to keep it in play and creates an inboard disposal or carrying option.

title: Collect, Turn and Exit
primarySkill: Changing direction efficiently after securing a ground ball
objective: Develop the ability to secure a ground ball, maintain a low and balanced position, and turn into a nominated exit without exposing or losing possession.
groundSize: Squares approximately ten metres × ten metres.
equipment: Coloured cards or cones for coach signals
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Create a ten-metre square.
Mark a collection point in the centre.
Position three coloured exit gates in front, left and right of the collection point.
The feeder stands four to five metres behind the collection point.
The collector begins five metres opposite the feeder.
The coach stands where all three gates can be seen.
The feeder rolls the football towards the centre.
The coach displays or calls an exit colour as the collector approaches.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder rolls the football towards the centre of the square.
The collector approaches and tracks the football.
Before collection, the coach nominates one of the three exit gates.
The player adjusts the feet and collects with two hands.
Possession is secured while the player remains low.
The player places the outside foot to support the required change of direction.
The hips and shoulders rotate towards the nominated gate.
The football is protected close to the body during the turn.
The player accelerates through the exit gate.
The collector becomes the feeder and the next player begins.
coachingPoints: Do not turn the body before the football is secured.
Maintain a strong base through the collection.
Keep the football close to the chest or protected hip.
Use active feet rather than twisting from a fixed position.
Place the outside foot firmly before changing direction.
Rotate the hips and shoulders together.
Keep the head and eyes up as the player exits.
Accelerate only after balance has been restored.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the player recognises the nominated gate.
Whether the collection remains the first priority.
Whether possession is secured before rotation.
Whether the feet support the change of direction.
Whether the player remains balanced and low.
Whether the football stays protected.
Whether the turn is completed without unnecessary steps.
Whether acceleration occurs through the gate.

commonErrors.error: The player turns before controlling the football.
commonErrors.correction: Complete two-hand possession before rotating towards the gate.

commonErrors.error: The collector twists from planted feet.
commonErrors.correction: Use adjustment steps and place the outside foot before turning.

commonErrors.error: The player stands upright during the change of direction.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain knee and hip flexion through the collection and turn.

commonErrors.error: The football is carried away from the body.
commonErrors.correction: Bring it immediately into a protected position.

commonErrors.error: The player crosses the feet and loses balance.
commonErrors.correction: Use short, stable steps and rotate from a strong base.

commonErrors.error: The collector looks down throughout the exit.
commonErrors.correction: Lift the eyes once possession is secure and scan through the gate.

progressions: Delay the exit call until the player is closer to the football.
Add a fourth gate behind the collection point.
Add a passive defender closing one gate.
Require an immediate handball or kick after the turn.
Increase the speed of the feed.
regressions: Nominate the exit before the repetition begins.
Place the football stationary at the collection point.
Allow the player to walk through the turn.
Remove the coach signal and alternate exits in sequence.
successIndicators: Maintain a low and balanced base.
matchApplication: Ground-ball winners rarely continue in a straight line. Players must often turn away from pressure, move inboard from the boundary or change direction towards a supporting teammate. Efficient footwork allows the player to retain possession while creating separation.

title: Pre-Collection Scan and Release
primarySkill: Scanning for a disposal option before collecting a ground ball
objective: Develop the habit of scanning before possession so players can collect a ground ball and release quickly to the correct supporting option without compromising ball security.
groundSize: Diamonds approximately twelve metres long and ten metres wide.
equipment: Two differently coloured bibs or markers
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Create a diamond with a feeder at one end and the collector opposite.
Position one receiver to the left and one to the right of the collection point.
Give each receiver a different coloured bib or marker.
The collector begins six metres from the collection point.
The feeder rolls the football towards the centre.
Before the football reaches the collector, one receiver raises a marker or steps into an active target gate.
The active receiver must communicate the player’s name.
Rotate players through feeder, collector and receiver roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The collector begins moving towards the football.
The feeder rolls it into the central collection area.
Before lowering fully, the collector scans left and right.
One receiver becomes active by raising a coloured marker and communicating.
The collector identifies the active option before taking possession.
The player returns the eyes to the football and collects with two hands.
Possession is secured and the body is brought into balance.
The collector handballs to the active receiver.
The receiver catches the handball and returns the football to the feeder.
Players rotate after three repetitions in each role.
coachingPoints: Scan early enough that the eyes can return to the football before collection.
Use brief head movement rather than staring away from the football.
Receivers must provide clear verbal and visual information.
Keep the final approach controlled while scanning.
Complete the ground-ball collection before beginning the handball.
Bring the football into a stable striking platform.
Release towards the receiver’s path rather than their starting position.
Continue supporting after the handball.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the collector scans before reaching the football.
Whether both potential receivers are recognised.
Whether the eyes return to the football before collection.
Whether scanning affects approach speed or balance.
Whether the collection remains clean.
Whether the correct receiver is selected.
Whether the handball is delivered accurately.
Whether receivers communicate early and continue moving.

commonErrors.error: The player does not scan until after collecting.
commonErrors.correction: Check both sides during the approach before lowering fully.

commonErrors.error: The collector looks away for too long and misses the football.
commonErrors.correction: Use a brief scan and return the eyes immediately to the collection.

commonErrors.error: The player chooses the loudest receiver without seeing the visual cue.
commonErrors.correction: Confirm both the communication and the active colour.

commonErrors.error: The handball begins before possession is secure.
commonErrors.correction: Complete the collection and establish a striking platform first.

commonErrors.error: The collector stops completely before scanning.
commonErrors.correction: Scan while approaching at controlled speed.

commonErrors.error: Receivers remain stationary and provide poor information.
commonErrors.correction: Move into the gate and communicate the collector’s name early.

progressions: Add a third receiver behind the collector.
Allow either handball or kick based on the receiver’s distance.
Add a passive defender closing one option.
Use a bouncing or angled feed.
Require the collector to continue supporting after disposal.
regressions: Nominate the receiver before the repetition.
Allow the collector to stop and scan.
Use a verbal cue without a colour signal.
successIndicators: Return their eyes to the football.
Release accurately to the correct option.
matchApplication: Players who gather first and scan later often hold the football too long or release under immediate pressure. Scanning during the approach allows the ground-ball winner to understand the surrounding options before possession and move the football quickly once control is established.

title: Non-Preferred-Side Pickup and Disposal
primarySkill: Preparing a non-preferred-side disposal after collecting a ground ball
objective: Develop the ability to collect a ground ball without transferring unnecessarily across the body and complete an accurate disposal towards the player’s non-preferred side.
groundSize: Lanes approximately fourteen metres long and eight metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Create a central collection lane with disposal targets positioned on both sides.
The feeder stands at one end and rolls the football towards the collector.
The collector begins five to seven metres away.
Identify each player’s preferred and non-preferred handball and kicking sides.
During the first block, use handball targets six to eight metres away.
During the second block, use short-kicking targets fifteen to twenty metres away.
The nominated target is placed on the player’s non-preferred side.
Rotate feeder and receiver roles regularly.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder rolls the football towards the collection area.
The collector approaches and positions the body behind its line.
The football is gathered cleanly with two hands.
The player remains balanced and keeps the football central.
The collector adjusts the feet towards the non-preferred-side target.
In the handball block, the player strikes with the non-preferred hand.
In the kicking block, the player transfers into a balanced non-preferred-foot kick.
The receiver presents through the target gate.
The player follows the disposal for two to three metres.
Roles rotate after four handballs and four kicks.
coachingPoints: The ground-ball collection must remain technically sound on both sides.
Keep the football central during the pickup.
Avoid carrying the football automatically towards the preferred side.
Move the feet to align the body with the target.
For handball, establish a stable platform and strike through the football.
For kicking, take sufficient balancing steps before the ball drop.
Use an appropriate disposal speed for the target distance.
Maintain accuracy rather than rushing to appear equally fast on both sides.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the collection remains clean.
Whether the football is brought centrally into possession.
Whether the player automatically shifts towards the preferred side.
Whether footwork creates alignment with the target.
Whether the non-preferred handball technique remains legal and controlled.
Whether the non-preferred kick has a stable ball drop.
Whether disposal accuracy is maintained.
Whether the player follows the football after release.

commonErrors.error: The player transfers the football across the body immediately after collection.
commonErrors.correction: Keep it central and move the feet towards the target.

commonErrors.error: The collector turns back onto the preferred side.
commonErrors.correction: Hold the nominated line and complete the non-preferred disposal.

commonErrors.error: The non-preferred handball is pushed rather than struck.
commonErrors.correction: Support the football and strike it cleanly with a closed fist.

commonErrors.error: The player kicks before regaining balance.
commonErrors.correction: Add controlled preparation steps before the ball drop.

commonErrors.error: The football is dropped from excessive height.
commonErrors.correction: Guide it lower and closer to the non-preferred foot.

commonErrors.error: Accuracy falls because the player rushes.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce speed and prioritise balanced technique.

progressions: Alternate preferred and non-preferred targets unpredictably.
Add a passive opponent blocking the preferred side.
Require the receiver to continue the possession chain.
successIndicators: Collect cleanly without favouring one side.
Align the feet with the non-preferred target.
matchApplication: Ground-ball winners cannot always return to their preferred side. Pressure, field position and teammate movement may require an immediate handball or kick in the opposite direction. Balanced collection and footwork allow the player to use the available option rather than turning back into pressure.

title: Controlled Knock-to-Advantage Recovery
primarySkill: Using a controlled touch to move an uncollectable ground ball into a recoverable position
objective: Teach players to recognise when immediate clean possession is unavailable and use a legal, controlled touch to move the football into space before completing the recovery.
groundSize: Lanes approximately twelve metres long and six metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Create a twelve-metre lane with a feeder at one end.
Place an obstacle cone or mannequin in front of the collection line.
Mark a recoverable space one to two metres to either side of the obstacle.
The collector begins six metres away.
The feeder rolls the football towards the obstacle.
On selected repetitions, the football is collectable immediately.
On other repetitions, the obstacle position makes a clean first pickup unrealistic.
The collector must decide whether to take possession or use a controlled touch around the obstacle.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder rolls the football towards the collection area.
The collector approaches and judges whether clean possession is available.
When the line is clear, the player collects with two hands and exits.
When the obstacle blocks the collection line, the player uses an open hand to tap the football one to two metres into the nominated recovery space.
The touch must remain controlled and within the player’s next running path.
The collector immediately changes line and follows the football.
The player reaches the new line from behind.
The football is secured with two hands.
The player exits through the corresponding recovery gate.
Players rotate through collector and feeder roles.
coachingPoints: Clean possession remains the preferred action whenever it is realistically available.
Make the decision early enough to control the first touch.
Use an open hand and direct the football rather than throwing or scooping it.
Touch the football into accessible space, not simply away from the obstacle.
Keep the first touch within one or two strides.
Continue moving immediately after contact.
Reposition the body behind the football for the second action.
Complete the recovery with two hands before accelerating.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the player correctly identifies a collectable football.
Whether unnecessary taps replace available clean possession.
