Mark a central ground-ball collection zone.
Position one support runner behind and left of the collector.
Position a second support runner behind and right.
Mark crossing lanes that pass behind or outside the collector before entering opposite exit gates.
Position the feeder behind the collection zone.
A coach displays a coloured marker that identifies which exit is restricted.
The collector must read the crossing runners and restricted gate.
Rotate all roles after each repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder rolls the football towards the central collection zone.
The collector approaches and scans both support runners.
Both runners accelerate on crossing lines.
The coach identifies one restricted exit gate.
The collector returns vision to the football and gathers cleanly.
The player protects possession while recognising which runner is moving towards the available gate.
The collector handballs into that runner’s path.
The receiver continues through the open exit.
The non-receiving runner becomes secondary support.
The original collector follows the possession through the middle.
coachingPoints: Scan the runner positions before lowering fully.
Support runners must cross with safe separation.
Return the eyes to the football before collection.
Secure possession before responding to the gate restriction.
Avoid predetermining the receiver.
Handball ahead of the runner rather than towards the crossing point.
The non-receiving runner must remain involved.
The collector should continue through the middle after disposal.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the collector scans both runners.
Whether the crossing movements are safely timed.
Whether the restricted gate is recognised.
Whether vision returns to the football.
Whether collection remains clean.
Whether the correct runner is selected.
Whether the handball leads the receiver.
Whether all players continue supporting.

commonErrors.error: The collector chooses a runner before reading the gate.
commonErrors.correction: Wait for the full information before releasing possession.

commonErrors.error: Support runners cross too closely.
commonErrors.correction: Stagger the crossing times and maintain safe separation.

commonErrors.error: The player watches the runners and fumbles the football.
commonErrors.correction: Scan briefly, then return the eyes to the collection.

commonErrors.error: The handball is directed at the crossing point.
commonErrors.correction: Target the receiver’s movement beyond the crossing line.

commonErrors.error: The non-receiving runner stops.
commonErrors.correction: Continue as a secondary option.

commonErrors.error: The collector remains behind the play.
commonErrors.correction: Follow through the middle after disposal.

progressions: Add a passive defender closing the collector.
Allow the collector to carry through the middle if both runners are covered.
Introduce turnover transition after an inaccurate handball.
regressions: Operate with one support runner before adding the second.
matchApplication: Crossing support runs can confuse defenders and create an exit from congestion. The ball winner must process several moving options while still prioritising a clean ground-ball collection.

title: Defensive 50 Ground-Ball Exit Pattern
primarySkill: Connecting a defensive 50 ground-ball recovery into a structured exit
objective: Develop a coordinated defensive 50 exit in which a ground-ball winner protects possession, connects with support and transfers the football towards a safer attacking lane.
groundSize: Approximately one-third of a full oval, including a defensive pocket, half-back flank and corridor exit lane.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Mark a ground-ball recovery zone in a defensive pocket.
Position a feeder or coach twenty metres away to send the football into the zone.
Place the ground-ball winner inside the pocket.
Position an inboard support player behind and inside the collection line.
Place a half-back outlet player wider and farther forward.
Position a corridor target near the edge of the defensive 50.
Add one passive pressure player approaching the initial contest.
Mark the intended running and disposal lanes clearly for the introductory repetitions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder sends a low kick or rolling football into the defensive pocket.
The ground-ball player approaches and secures possession.
The passive pressure player closes from the boundary side.
The inboard support player presents through the first gate.
The collector handballs to the inboard support player and follows.
The receiver carries forward and connects with the half-back outlet.
The half-back player scans the corridor target.
The football is kicked or handballed into the corridor exit lane.
All players move forward to support the next phase.
The group resets and rotates positions.
coachingPoints: Protect the boundary side of the initial collection.
Scan inboard before reaching the football.
Support players must begin behind the football.
The first handball should lead the receiver away from pressure.
The original ground-ball winner follows to support.
Half-back width should be maintained until the disposal is released.
Enter the corridor only when the target is clearly available.
Every possession should gain field position or improve the team’s shape.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the initial ground-ball collection is secure.
Whether the collector uses the body against boundary-side pressure.
Whether the inboard support begins behind the football.
Whether the first handball improves field position.
Whether the original collector follows the play.
Whether half-back width is preserved.
Whether the corridor target presents at the correct time.
Whether all players transition forward after disposal.

commonErrors.error: The collector turns towards the boundary under pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Position the body boundary side and prepare the inboard exit.

commonErrors.error: Support players begin ahead of the football.
commonErrors.correction: Start behind and move through as possession is won.

commonErrors.error: The first handball is delivered sideways or backwards without purpose.
commonErrors.correction: Lead the receiver forward and away from pressure.

commonErrors.error: The original collector stops after disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Follow the handball to support the next phase.

commonErrors.error: The half-back outlet moves into congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Hold width until the possession chain reaches the outlet.

commonErrors.error: The corridor kick is forced when the target is unavailable.
commonErrors.correction: Retain possession or use the wider outlet.

progressions: Add a turnover consequence and forward-entry response.
regressions: Walk through the complete pattern before increasing speed.
successIndicators: Connect cleanly through the inboard outlet.
Move forward together after the exit.
matchApplication: Defensive ground-ball recoveries are high-risk possessions because poor body position or disposal can create a direct scoring opportunity. A structured exit gives the ball winner immediate support and moves possession away from the dangerous pocket area.
relatedDrills: GB-028 – Ground-Ball Release and Second Involvement
GB-035 – Wide Ground-Ball Win to Corridor Switch
GB-032 – Retreating Recovery and Forward Exit

title: Ground-Ball Movement Competency Assessment
primarySkill: Assessing ground-ball collection and execution while moving through varied football situations
objective: Assess each player’s ability to collect ground balls while moving, maintain balance and momentum, connect with support and complete an effective post-collection action.
groundSize: Six assessment stations arranged within an area approximately fifty metres × forty metres.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Establish six assessment stations:
Station 1: Running-through collection and acceleration.
Station 2: Angled or crossing-line collection.
Station 3: Retreating recovery and forward exit.
Station 4: Scan and release to moving support.
Station 5: Carry, running bounce and kick.
Station 6: Structured wide-to-corridor movement.
Divide players evenly between stations.
Assign a coach or trained observer to each station.
Give each player two familiarisation repetitions before scoring begins.
Record outcomes using consistent technical and decision-making criteria.
Assess both preferred and non-preferred movement directions.
Allow appropriate recovery between high-speed repetitions.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players complete the stations in numerical order.
Each player performs three scored repetitions at every station.
Coaches assess the collection, movement before possession, post-collection action and disposal outcome.
A repetition begins when the feeder releases the football.
Players must respond to the station’s movement or decision requirement without additional coaching.
Each repetition ends when the player exits the finishing gate or the target controls the disposal.
Coaches record the score immediately.
Players rotate after all group members complete the station.
Failed repetitions are not repeated unless equipment or feeder error affected the outcome.
Results are reviewed after the complete rotation.
coachingPoints: Use the same feed standards for all players.
Assess the player’s movement before possession, not only the final pickup.
Record whether the player reaches the football’s line.
Evaluate balance and ball security after collection.
Assess scanning and option selection where required.
Record the accuracy and timing of the disposal.
Distinguish technical errors from decision-making errors.
Avoid providing corrective coaching during scored repetitions.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Approach speed and running-line adjustment.
Body position at the moment of collection.
Use of two hands where clean possession is available.
Balance and momentum after collection.
Pre-collection scanning.
Support recognition and disposal choice.
Ball-carrying control.
Disposal timing and accuracy.

commonErrors.error: Feeds vary significantly between players.
commonErrors.correction: Use defined starting positions, speeds and target zones for every repetition.

commonErrors.error: The observer scores only whether the player collected the football.
commonErrors.correction: Assess the complete sequence before, during and after possession.

commonErrors.error: Coaching feedback is given during scored repetitions.
commonErrors.correction: Record the outcome and provide feedback after the station is completed.

commonErrors.error: Players are assessed from one movement direction only.
commonErrors.correction: Include left, right, forward and retreating movement demands.

commonErrors.error: Fatigue affects later scores disproportionately.
commonErrors.correction: Schedule recovery and balance high-load stations across the circuit.

commonErrors.error: Scores are recorded without supporting comments.
commonErrors.correction: Add a brief technical or decision-making observation for each station.

progressions: Add controlled defensive pressure at selected stations.
Use wet footballs in safe conditions.
Compare results across multiple assessment dates.
regressions: Reduce the number of assessed stations.
Use two scored repetitions per station.
Complete a coached practice block before formal assessment.
successIndicators: Adjust their approach to different football movements.
Maintain technical quality across the complete assessment.
matchApplication: Ground-ball performance depends on more than the initial pickup. Players must reach loose footballs from different directions, retain balance, identify support and execute the next action. This assessment identifies whether those movement skills transfer across varied Australian football situations.
relatedDrills: GB-032 – Retreating Recovery and Forward Exit
GB-035 – Wide Ground-Ball Win to Corridor Switch

title: Trailing-Pressure Ground-Ball Pickup
primarySkill: Collecting a ground ball while maintaining separation from trailing pressure
objective: Develop the ability to collect a ground ball cleanly while an opponent applies controlled pressure from behind, then accelerate away without exposing possession.
groundSize: Lanes approximately eighteen metres long and six metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Create an eighteen-metre lane with a three-metre collection zone in the middle.
Position the collector eight metres from the collection zone.
Position the pressure player one to two metres behind the collector.
Place the feeder beside the collection zone.
Mark a finishing gate five metres beyond the collection point.
The pressure player may shadow, reach towards the football and apply light shoulder proximity but may not tackle.
Rotate collector, pressure player and feeder roles after each repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder rolls the football into the collection zone.
The collector and pressure player begin on the feeder’s release.
The collector accelerates towards the football while recognising the opponent’s position.
The player adjusts the running line to place the body between the opponent and the football.
The collector shortens the final steps and gathers with two hands.
The football is brought immediately into a protected position.
The collector accelerates through the finishing gate.
The pressure player continues shadowing without tackling.
A repetition is successful when the collector retains possession through the gate.
Players rotate roles and repeat from the opposite side of the lane.
coachingPoints: Win the race to the football without arriving out of control.
Use the running line to prevent the opponent reaching directly beside the football.
Keep the hips and knees flexed through collection.
Gather with two hands whenever clean possession is available.
Bring the football immediately to the protected side.
Do not slow excessively and invite the opponent back into the contest.
Accelerate after possession is secured.
Remain balanced if incidental shoulder contact occurs.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the collector reacts quickly to the feed.
Whether the running line protects the football.
Whether the player remains under control near the collection.
Whether the pressure player applies realistic but safe pressure.
Whether the football is collected with two hands.
Whether possession is protected immediately.
Whether the collector accelerates after winning the football.
Whether the player maintains balance under incidental contact.

commonErrors.error: The collector runs beside the football and allows the opponent direct access.
commonErrors.correction: Adjust the line earlier and place the body between the opponent and the football.

commonErrors.error: The player approaches at uncontrolled speed.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the final steps before lowering into the pickup.

commonErrors.error: The collector reaches with one hand because pressure is close.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain two-hand collection unless the football is genuinely uncollectable.

commonErrors.error: The football remains exposed after collection.
commonErrors.correction: Bring it immediately to the chest or protected hip.

commonErrors.error: The player slows after securing possession.
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate through the finishing gate.

commonErrors.error: The pressure player tackles despite the restriction.
commonErrors.correction: Return to shadow pressure and reinforce the contact rule.

progressions: Reduce the pressure player’s starting deficit.
Allow controlled tackling after possession is established.
Roll the football slightly across the collector’s path.
Require an immediate handball after the exit.
regressions: Increase the pressure player’s starting deficit.
Restrict the pressure player to shadow running only.
successIndicators: Position the body between opponent and football.
matchApplication: Players often approach loose footballs with an opponent closing from behind. Using the body line before possession allows the player to collect cleanly and prevents the opponent from reaching the football or applying an immediate tackle.
relatedDrills: GB-024 – Collect and Evade Exit Gates

title: Front-On Pressure Ground-Ball Win
primarySkill: Winning a ground ball against an opponent approaching from the opposite direction
objective: Develop the ability to remain low, protect the head and body, and secure a ground ball when an opponent approaches from the opposite direction under controlled contact conditions.
groundSize: Contest channels approximately ten metres long and five metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a central contest zone two metres long.
Position one player five metres from each side of the zone.
Place the football in the centre or have a coach roll it into the zone.
Mark an exit gate behind each player’s starting position.
Players compete to secure possession and exit through either side gate.
Contact is restricted to legal shoulder-to-shoulder bodywork.
Front-on contact to the head, neck or player over the football is prohibited.
Pair players by size, skill and contact readiness.
howTheDrillWorks:
Both players begin on the coach’s signal.
The players approach the football from opposite directions.
Each player controls the final steps and lowers the body.
Players compete to establish the strongest line to the football.
The first player with clean access attempts a two-hand collection.
Legal shoulder-to-shoulder contact may occur before possession.
Once possession is secured, the ball winner protects the football and exits through either gate.
The opponent applies controlled chase pressure without tackling in the introductory version.
The repetition ends when the player exits or the football leaves the channel.
Players reset and alternate starting sides.
coachingPoints: Keep the head and eyes up during the approach.
Lower through the knees and hips rather than leading with the head.
Approach slightly off-centre to avoid dangerous head-on contact.
Use the shoulder and hip to hold a legal line.
Keep the feet active through the contest.
Secure the football with two hands when possible.
Protect possession immediately after winning it.
Exit laterally rather than attempting to run through the opponent.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players approach with safe body height.
Whether heads remain out of the direct contact line.
Whether contact is legal and controlled.
Whether players use shoulder and hip positioning.
Whether feet remain active.
Whether the football is collected rather than knocked away unnecessarily.
Whether the winner protects possession.
Whether the exit moves away from the opponent.

commonErrors.error: Players approach directly head-on.
commonErrors.correction: Use a slight angle and keep the head outside the opponent’s line.

commonErrors.error: A player bends from the waist and leads with the head.
commonErrors.correction: Lower through the knees and hips with the chest balanced.

commonErrors.error: Contact is made high or front-on.
commonErrors.correction: Restrict contact to legal shoulder-to-shoulder bodywork.

commonErrors.error: Players stop their feet at the contest.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain short, active steps through the football.

commonErrors.error: The football is slapped away despite clean access.
commonErrors.correction: Prioritise possession when two-hand collection is available.

commonErrors.error: The winner attempts to run directly through the opponent.
commonErrors.correction: Protect the football and exit laterally into space.

progressions: Roll the football into the contest from different angles.
Add a support player for each contestant.
Reduce the width of the exit gates.
Introduce a scoring system for clean possession and effective exit.
regressions: Use bump pads before live body contact.
Predetermine which player has the inside line.
Allow one player to apply shadow pressure only.
Start players closer to the contest zone.
successIndicators: Keep the head outside the contact line.
Establish a strong legal body position.
matchApplication: Opponents frequently arrive at loose footballs from opposite directions. Safe, low and legally positioned bodywork allows a player to compete strongly without exposing the head or conceding possession through poor balance.
relatedDrills: GB-024 – Collect and Evade Exit Gates

title: Shoulder-to-Shoulder Ground-Ball Contest
primarySkill: Maintaining body position in a shoulder-to-shoulder race for a loose football
objective: Develop the ability to use legal shoulder-to-shoulder body positioning while running alongside an opponent, win access to the football and complete a clean collection.
groundSize: Lanes approximately fifteen metres long and six metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position two players side by side at paired starting cones.
Mark a collection zone eight to ten metres ahead.
The feeder stands beside the lane and rolls the football forward.
The football should remain inside the lane and be collectable by either player.
Players may use legal shoulder-to-shoulder contact while running.
Holding, pushing in the back, blocking with extended arms and high contact are prohibited.
Place a finishing line three metres beyond the collection zone.
Pair players appropriately for size and experience.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder rolls the football into the lane.
Both players accelerate from their starting positions.
Each player attempts to establish the inside line.
Legal shoulder-to-shoulder contact may be used while both players remain upright.
The player gaining the better line controls the final steps.
The player lowers and collects with two hands.
The opponent continues controlled pressure without tackling.
The ball winner carries possession across the finishing line.
One point is awarded for clean possession and one for retaining the football through the line.
Players alternate starting sides after each repetition.
coachingPoints: Track the football while maintaining awareness of the opponent.
Use the shoulder and hip rather than extended arms.
Keep the feet moving through body contact.
Avoid leaning so heavily that running balance is lost.
Work towards the inside line before the collection point.
Reduce speed enough to collect cleanly.
Bring the football immediately to the protected side.
Accelerate once possession is secure.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players use legal body contact.
Whether running balance is maintained.
Whether extended arms are avoided.
Whether either player establishes the inside line.
Whether the final approach remains controlled.
Whether the football is collected cleanly.
Whether the ball winner protects possession.
Whether the opponent respects the no-tackle restriction.

commonErrors.error: The player pushes with an extended arm.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the arm close and use legal shoulder-to-shoulder bodywork.

commonErrors.error: The player leans excessively and loses balance.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain the feet underneath the body and apply controlled pressure.

commonErrors.error: Both players focus only on contact and lose the football.
commonErrors.correction: Keep vision on the football while using peripheral awareness.

commonErrors.error: The player reaches down at full speed.
commonErrors.correction: Control the final steps before collecting.

commonErrors.error: The winner carries the football on the opponent’s side.
commonErrors.correction: Bring it immediately to the protected side.

commonErrors.error: The pressure player tackles after the collection.
commonErrors.correction: Continue shadow pressure only until tackling is introduced as a progression.

progressions: Begin with one player slightly behind.
Require an immediate handball to a supporting teammate.
Add a boundary line on one side of the lane.
regressions: Use shoulder-contact walk-throughs before adding the football.
Give one player a clear inside-line advantage.
successIndicators: Protect or regain the inside line.
Protect and carry through the finishing line.
matchApplication: Loose footballs often create running contests in which players arrive side by side. Legal body positioning can deny an opponent direct access while allowing the player to stay balanced and complete the collection.

title: Ground-Ball Shield and Escape
primarySkill: Protecting possession after winning a ground ball in close pressure
objective: Develop the ability to secure a ground ball, place the body between the football and opponent, and escape through an available exit under controlled contact pressure.
groundSize: Squares approximately ten metres × ten metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a central collection zone.
Position the collector four metres from the football.
Position the defender one metre behind and slightly to one side.
Mark three exit gates ahead, left and right.
The coach nominates one closed gate immediately before collection.
The defender may apply controlled body pressure but may not tackle in the introductory version.
The collector must secure possession and escape through an available gate.
Rotate roles after each repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach signals the start and identifies the closed gate.
The collector approaches the football with the defender following.
The collector positions the body between the opponent and football.
The football is gathered with two hands.
The player brings possession immediately to the protected side.
The defender applies controlled shoulder or hip pressure.
The collector uses short steps, body strength and an angled turn to reach an open gate.
The player accelerates through the gate.
The repetition ends when the collector exits or possession is lost.
Players alternate roles and starting sides.
coachingPoints: Establish protection before touching the football.
Keep a strong, low base through collection.
Secure possession with two hands before transferring it to the protected side.
Use the shoulder, back and hips legally to shield the opponent.
Keep the feet active under pressure.
Avoid turning blindly into the defender.
Select the exit that moves away from pressure.
Accelerate once separation has been created.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the collector establishes body position early.
Whether the collection remains clean.
Whether possession is moved to the protected side.
Whether the defender applies safe, legal pressure.
Whether the collector keeps the feet active.
Whether the player scans the available gates.
Whether the exit moves away from the opponent.
Whether acceleration occurs after separation.

commonErrors.error: The player collects before establishing protection.
commonErrors.correction: Place the body between the opponent and football before lowering the hands.

commonErrors.error: The football remains exposed in front of the body.
commonErrors.correction: Bring it to the chest or far hip immediately.

commonErrors.error: The collector stops the feet under pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Use short, continuous steps to maintain balance and create an exit.

commonErrors.error: The player turns directly into the defender.
commonErrors.correction: Scan the pressure side and rotate towards open space.

commonErrors.error: The defender pushes in the back or holds.
commonErrors.correction: Restrict pressure to legal shoulder and hip contact.

commonErrors.error: The collector attempts to break contact without securing possession.
commonErrors.correction: Control the football first, then accelerate away.

progressions: Add a support player as an alternative handball exit.
Begin with the defender level rather than behind.
Add a second defender applying shadow pressure.
regressions: Use a bump pad instead of a live defender.
successIndicators: Secure the football on the protected side.
matchApplication: Winning the ground ball is only the first part of the contest. Players must often absorb pressure immediately after collection and use body position and footwork to retain possession long enough to escape or dispose effectively.
relatedDrills: GB-024 – Collect and Evade Exit Gates

title: Knock-to-Teammate Under Pressure
primarySkill: Directing an uncollectable football to a supporting teammate under pressure
objective: Develop the ability to recognise when clean possession is unavailable and legally direct the football towards a better-positioned teammate without losing involvement in the contest.
groundSize: Rectangles approximately fifteen metres long and ten metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a central contest zone.
Position one contestant and one defender on opposite sides of the football.
Place one support teammate five metres to the left and another five metres to the right.
One support player becomes active and communicates before the contest.
The coach rolls the football into a position where immediate clean collection is difficult.
The contestant may use an open hand, fist or legal tap to direct the football.
The defender applies controlled body pressure without tackling the support receiver.
Rotate all roles after each repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach rolls the football into the contest zone.
The active support player communicates and moves through a support gate.
The contestant and defender approach the football.
The contestant judges whether clean possession is realistically available.
When possession is unavailable, the player uses a controlled touch to direct the football towards the active teammate.
The support player gathers and exits the contest area.
The original contestant continues forward to shepherd, support or receive a return handball.
The defender applies controlled chase pressure.
A successful repetition requires the supporting team to retain possession through an exit gate.
Players rotate roles and change support sides.
coachingPoints: Clean possession remains the first option when available.
Identify the support player before entering the contest.
Direct the football into the teammate’s path rather than merely knocking it away.
Keep the touch legal and brief.
Use body position to protect the direction of the tap.
Follow the football immediately after the touch.
Support players must communicate early and remain outside congestion.
Continue contributing after the teammate gains possession.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the player distinguishes between collectable and uncollectable footballs.
Whether support communication occurs early.
Whether the touch is legal and controlled.
Whether the football is directed towards the teammate’s path.
Whether the defender applies realistic pressure.
Whether the contestant follows the football.
Whether the support player gathers cleanly.
Whether possession is retained through the exit.

commonErrors.error: The player taps a football that could be collected.
commonErrors.correction: Prioritise clean possession when two-hand control is available.

commonErrors.error: The football is knocked randomly away.
commonErrors.correction: Identify the support target and direct the touch into their path.

commonErrors.error: The tap becomes a scoop or throw.
commonErrors.correction: Use brief legal contact without carrying the football.

commonErrors.error: The contestant stops after the touch.
commonErrors.correction: Follow immediately and provide protection or support.

commonErrors.error: Support players remain too close to congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Hold width and move through the nominated support gate.

commonErrors.error: The defender targets the support player before the touch.
commonErrors.correction: Defend the contesting player until possession transfers.

progressions: Allow either support player to become active.
Permit controlled tackling after the support player collects.
Require a return handball to the original contestant.
regressions: Rehearse the directional tap without pressure.
Increase the distance between defender and contestant.
Allow the support player to begin closer.
successIndicators: Recognise whether clean possession is available.
matchApplication: In congested football, the first player may be unable to take clean possession. A controlled knock or tap to a teammate can preserve the team’s advantage, provided it is purposeful and followed by an immediate second effort.

title: Congested Box Ground-Ball Extraction
primarySkill: Securing and extracting a ground ball from a confined space
objective: Develop the ability to win a loose football in a confined area, protect possession and release accurately to a teammate positioned outside congestion.
groundSize: Central contest box approximately six metres × six metres with a surrounding twelve-metre square.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a six-metre central contest box.
Place two players from opposing teams inside the box.
Position one receiver from each team outside opposite sides of the box.
The coach stands on the boundary of the box with footballs.
The coach rolls or drops the football into different locations inside the box.
Inside players may use legal controlled bodywork.
Tackling is restricted to wrapping and holding without taking players to ground.
An extraction is completed when the football reaches a teammate outside the box.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach introduces the football into the contest box.
Both inside players compete for position and possession.
The player winning access attempts a two-hand collection.
The ball winner protects possession from the opponent.
Outside receivers move laterally and communicate.
The ball winner may carry within the box or handball immediately.
The player handballs through a receiver gate to a teammate.
If possession spills, both inside players continue competing.
The repetition ends when a receiver controls the football or it leaves the area.
Inside and outside players rotate after three repetitions.
coachingPoints: Enter the contest with a low, balanced body position.
Keep the head protected and outside the opponent’s direct contact line.
Use the hips and shoulders to establish space.
Secure the football before attempting to dispose.
Keep the feet moving after possession.
Outside receivers should provide clear, changing targets.
Handball towards space outside the congestion.
Continue supporting after the extraction.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players enter the contest safely.
Whether legal body positioning is used.
Whether the football is secured rather than repeatedly knocked away.
Whether the ball winner remains balanced.
Whether outside receivers communicate and move.
Whether the handball exits congestion.
Whether restricted tackling remains controlled.
Whether players continue after a spill.

commonErrors.error: Players dive head-first into congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Lower with the head protected and enter on a balanced line.

commonErrors.error: The ball winner stops the feet.
commonErrors.correction: Keep stepping to maintain balance and create a release angle.

commonErrors.error: The player handballs before controlling the football.
commonErrors.correction: Secure possession before beginning the striking action.

commonErrors.error: Outside receivers remain stationary.
commonErrors.correction: Move around the box and create a visible target.

commonErrors.error: The handball remains inside congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Direct the disposal through an outside gate.

commonErrors.error: Tackles pull players to ground.
commonErrors.correction: Restrict contact to controlled wrapping and holding.

progressions: Play two versus two inside the box.
Allow full controlled tackling for appropriate groups.
Introduce a time limit for extraction.
Continue into a short possession game after the release.
regressions: Use one active contestant and one shadow defender.
Roll the football towards one player.
Allow the ball winner to exit by carrying.
matchApplication: Stoppages and compressed contests require players to win football in limited space and move it to teammates positioned outside. Successful extraction depends on body strength, ball security and awareness of the release option.
relatedDrills: HB-049 – Ground-Ball Win and Handball Exit

title: Smothered-Disposal Recovery Contest
primarySkill: Reacting to and winning the football immediately after a disposal is smothered
objective: Develop the ability to react immediately after a smothered disposal, regain balance and compete for the resulting loose football before completing an effective next action.
groundSize: Channels approximately twelve metres long and eight metres wide.

primarySkill: Using a third-player receiver arriving after the initial ground-ball contest forms
objective: Develop the ability to engage pressure inside a ground-ball contest and release to a third player arriving outside the immediate congestion.
groundSize: Rectangles approximately twenty metres long and fifteen metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Position one attacker and one defender inside a six-metre contest box.
Position a second attacker near the edge of the box as immediate support.
Position a third attacker five metres behind a delayed-receiver gate.
Add a second defender who may pressure the immediate support player.
The third attacker cannot move until the ball winner secures possession.
Mark a forward finishing gate beyond the congestion.
Controlled tackling is permitted inside the box.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach introduces the football into the contest box.
The inside attacker and defender compete for possession.
The immediate support player moves to attract the second defender.
Once possession is secured, the third player accelerates through the delayed gate.
The ball winner protects possession and recognises the late runner.
The football is handballed beyond congestion to the third player.
The third player receives facing forward.
The immediate support player and original ball winner continue running.
The attacking group exits through the finishing gate.
If possession changes, defenders counterattack towards the opposite side.
coachingPoints: The first two attackers must engage the inside defenders.
The third player must remain outside until possession is established.
Time the delayed run to arrive after defenders commit.
The ball winner should protect possession rather than release blindly.
Handball beyond the congestion line.
The third player should receive at speed and facing forward.
Immediate support remains involved even when not receiving.
All players transition after turnover.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether inside players engage the defenders.
Whether the third player delays movement.
Whether the run begins when possession is secured.
Whether the ball winner identifies the late receiver.
Whether the handball clears congestion.
Whether the receiver gathers at speed.
Whether non-receiving attackers continue supporting.
Whether defenders transition after turnover.

commonErrors.error: The third player enters congestion before possession.
commonErrors.correction: Hold outside until the ball winner secures the football.

commonErrors.error: The immediate support player does not attract a defender.
commonErrors.correction: Present visibly and create a genuine threat.

commonErrors.error: The ball winner releases before seeing the late runner.
commonErrors.correction: Protect possession and respond to communication.

commonErrors.error: The handball remains inside the contest box.
commonErrors.correction: Deliver beyond congestion into forward space.

commonErrors.error: The third player receives while stationary.
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate through the gate and show the hands early.

commonErrors.error: Non-receiving attackers stop after the release.
commonErrors.correction: Continue running as support and turnover cover.

progressions: Add a final kick to a leading target.
regressions: Allow the third player to begin closer.
Pause briefly after possession before the run starts.
matchApplication: A third player arriving after a contest forms can exploit defenders who have committed to the initial ball winner and immediate support. This creates a clean forward-facing release from congestion.

title: Ground-Ball Exit Risk Matrix
primarySkill: Selecting a corridor, wide or retention exit according to pressure, support and field risk
objective: Develop the ability to select the highest-value realistic exit after a ground-ball win rather than automatically choosing the fastest or most direct option.
groundSize: Area approximately thirty metres long and twenty-five metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Mark a central ground-ball contest area.
Create a narrow corridor gate worth three points.
Create two wide gates worth two points.
Create a rear retention gate worth one point.
Position attackers in each support lane.
Place defenders in different starting arrangements before each repetition.
The team winning possession chooses any exit.
A turnover deducts two points.
Controlled tackling is permitted.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach arranges defenders in a visible structure.
The football is introduced into the central contest.
Players compete for possession.
The ball winner and support players assess the available exits.
The attacking team attempts to use the highest-value realistic option.
The corridor scores three points when completed without turnover.
A wide exit scores two points.
Rear retention scores one point when forward exits are unsafe.
A turnover deducts two points and allows the opposition to counterattack.
Teams complete a set number of repetitions before changing roles.
coachingPoints: Point value does not override the actual defensive picture.
Scan support and opposition numbers before possession.
The corridor is valuable only when the receiver has an advantage.
Wide exits should gain territory rather than merely move sideways.
Rear retention is appropriate when forward risk is excessive.
Support players must hold their lanes.
The first disposal should clear immediate pressure.
Review both the decision and execution separately.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players scan all exit lanes.
Whether they understand the scoring values.
Whether high-risk corridor attempts are forced.
Whether wide receivers maintain spacing.
Whether rear support remains available.
Whether decisions reflect defensive positioning.
Whether execution matches the selected option.
Whether teams transition after turnover.

commonErrors.error: Players force the corridor because it scores more.
commonErrors.correction: Select the highest-value option that is genuinely available.

commonErrors.error: Wide receivers move into the central contest.
commonErrors.correction: Hold lane width and preserve the two-point exit.

commonErrors.error: Rear support is ignored when all forward options close.
commonErrors.correction: Use retention rather than conceding a turnover.

commonErrors.error: Players choose the safest option every time.
commonErrors.correction: Attack higher-value space when numbers and time provide an advantage.

commonErrors.error: The decision is correct but disposal execution is rushed.
commonErrors.correction: Secure possession and complete the skill in balance.

commonErrors.error: Defenders remain in the same structure every repetition.
commonErrors.correction: Vary denial patterns so attackers must re-assess.

progressions: Hide defender starting positions until the football is released.
Continue into a second attacking phase after exit.
regressions: Pause after possession for a brief scan.
Mark the preferred receiver with a coloured bib.
successIndicators: Avoid forcing high-value but closed options.
matchApplication: Ground-ball exits carry different levels of reward and risk. Elite players recognise when the corridor can be attacked, when width is required and when retaining possession is more valuable than forcing forward movement.
relatedDrills: GB-073 – Ground-Ball Win to Behind-the-Football Support
GB-077 – Ground-Ball Exit Against Corridor Denial

title: Disrupted Possession Re-Gather
primarySkill: Recovering possession after the initial ground-ball collection is disrupted
objective: Develop the ability to respond immediately when an opponent jars, deflects or partially dislodges the football after collection and complete a second secure possession action.
groundSize: Contest lanes approximately fourteen metres long and eight metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position the collector six metres from the initial collection zone.
Position the defender one metre behind or beside the collector.
The feeder rolls the football into the first zone.
After the collector secures possession, the defender applies a controlled bump, wrap or hand contact designed to disrupt but not dangerously strip the football.
Mark a surrounding recovery zone and two exit gates.
The collector must respond to any spill and regain possession.
Rotate collector, defender and feeder roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder releases the football.
The collector gathers and protects possession.
The defender applies controlled disruption after possession is established.
If the football remains secure, the collector exits immediately.
If it spills, both players locate the football.
The collector attempts to recover body position and complete a second pickup.
The defender competes under controlled contact rules.
The ball winner exits through either gate.
A point is awarded for retaining the first possession and a point for winning the re-gather after a spill.
Players rotate after three repetitions.
coachingPoints: Expect the contest to continue after the first collection.
Bring the football into a protected position immediately.
Maintain balance through the initial contact.
If possession spills, locate the football before reaching.
Recover the feet whenever possible.
Re-establish body position between opponent and football.
Treat the second action as a new ground-ball contest.
Avoid frustration after losing the first possession.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the initial collection is clean.
Whether the football is protected.
Whether contact remains safe.
Whether the collector reacts immediately to a spill.
Whether the player recovers balance.
Whether the football is located visually.
Whether body position is re-established.
Whether the second collection is secure.

commonErrors.error: The collector relaxes after the first pickup.
commonErrors.correction: Expect immediate pressure and secure the football strongly.

commonErrors.error: The defender strikes down dangerously at the arms.
commonErrors.correction: Use controlled body or wrapping pressure only.

commonErrors.error: The collector reaches blindly after the spill.
commonErrors.correction: Locate the football before re-entering the contest.

commonErrors.error: The player remains on the ground unnecessarily.
commonErrors.correction: Recover to the feet where safe and compete again.

commonErrors.error: The collector becomes frustrated after losing possession.
commonErrors.correction: Reset immediately and attack the next action.

commonErrors.error: Both players dive head-first at the spill.
commonErrors.correction: Approach with eyes up and safe body position.

progressions: Increase the unpredictability of the disruption.
Add a support player for each contestant.
Continue into a short transition phase.
Add fatigue before the initial collection.
regressions: Allow only the collector to recover initially.
matchApplication: Possession is frequently disrupted after a player initially wins a ground ball. Players who react immediately and treat the spill as a new contest are more likely to retain the football or prevent clean opposition transition.

title: Ground-Ball Tempo Control
primarySkill: Controlling the tempo of possession after a ground-ball win
objective: Develop the ability to decide whether to accelerate, hold possession briefly or reset after collecting a ground ball, according to pressure and teammate positioning.
groundSize: Rectangles approximately twenty-five metres long and eighteen metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Mark a central ground-ball collection zone.
Position one forward receiver, one lateral support player and one rear support player.
Add two defenders with variable starting positions.
Mark a fast exit gate, a short hold zone and a rear reset gate.
The coach changes defender positions before each repetition.
The ball winner must choose whether to accelerate immediately, hold for support or reset.
Controlled tackling is permitted.
Rotate all roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach introduces the football into the central zone.
The collector secures possession under pressure.
The collector scans the location of defenders and support.
When forward space is open, the player accelerates through the fast gate.
When support is developing but not yet available, the player protects possession inside the hold zone.
When forward and lateral exits are closed, the player uses rear support.
The attacking group continues possession through a finishing gate.
Defenders attempt to force rushed tempo or a turnover.
If possession changes, defenders counterattack.
The coach reviews whether the chosen tempo matched the situation.
coachingPoints: Fast play is valuable only when space and support are ready.
Holding possession means protecting and moving, not standing still.
Rear support provides a controlled reset.
Scan before and after collection.
Keep the football protected while waiting.
Change speed decisively once the option appears.
Avoid slowing when a clear advantage exists.
Evaluate the quality of the decision separately from the result.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the collector scans the defensive picture.
Whether immediate acceleration is selected appropriately.
Whether holding possession creates a better option.
Whether the player remains active while holding.
Whether rear support is used when required.
Whether the football remains protected.
Whether tempo changes decisively.
Whether the final disposal is completed in balance.

commonErrors.error: The player accelerates into closed space.
commonErrors.correction: Recognise pressure and hold or reset.

commonErrors.error: The collector slows despite a clear forward advantage.
commonErrors.correction: Attack immediately before defenders recover.

commonErrors.error: The player stands stationary in the hold zone.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the feet moving and protect possession.

commonErrors.error: Rear support is ignored.
commonErrors.correction: Use the reset when forward and lateral options are denied.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier waits too long after an option appears.
commonErrors.correction: Change speed and release immediately.

commonErrors.error: Defenders apply the same pressure pattern repeatedly.
commonErrors.correction: Vary starting positions and closing angles.

progressions: Allow defenders to change pressure after collection.
regressions: Pause after collection for a scan.
Use coloured cues for fast, hold or reset.
matchApplication: Not every ground-ball win should be moved at maximum speed. Elite players recognise when to exploit immediate space, when to protect possession while support arrives and when to reset rather than concede a turnover.

title: Dynamic Numbers Ground-Ball Game
primarySkill: Adapting ground-ball support and defensive roles as player numbers change during play
objective: Develop the ability to identify changing numerical advantage or disadvantage and reorganise contest, support and defensive roles without stopping play.
groundSize: Rectangle approximately forty metres long and thirty metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into two teams.
Begin with three players from each team inside the area.
Position additional players at interchange gates.
The coach restarts each phase with a ground ball.
During play, the coach displays a number or colour directing one or more players to enter or leave.
Numbers may change from three-versus-three to four-versus-three, three-versus-two or four-versus-four.
Teams score by carrying or disposing into their attacking end zone.
Controlled tackling is permitted.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach introduces a ground ball into the playing area.
Teams compete for possession.
Players organise contest and outside roles according to current numbers.
During possession, the coach changes player numbers.
Entering players must recognise whether to support, defend or remain behind the football.
Exiting players leave through the nearest interchange gate without disrupting play.
The possession team attempts to use any numerical advantage.
The defending team attempts to protect dangerous space while outnumbered.
If possession changes, roles reverse immediately.
Play continues for timed blocks with new ground-ball restarts after scores or stoppages.
coachingPoints: Count numbers before entering the contest.
Numerical advantage should create width, not extra congestion.
When outnumbered, protect the corridor and delay possession.
Entering players should not automatically run to the football.
Maintain one player behind possession when possible.
Communicate number changes immediately.
Use the first disposal to exploit the new shape.
Transition instantly when possession changes.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players recognise the numerical change.
Whether extra attackers create width.
Whether outnumbered defenders protect dangerous space.
Whether entering players select appropriate roles.
Whether players leaving the area do so safely.
Whether the first disposal exploits the changed numbers.
Whether support behind the football is maintained.
Whether transition occurs immediately after turnovers.

commonErrors.error: Extra attackers run directly to the contest.
commonErrors.correction: Use the numerical advantage to create outside options.

commonErrors.error: Outnumbered defenders chase the football individually.
commonErrors.correction: Protect the corridor and delay until support arrives.

commonErrors.error: Players fail to communicate the number change.
commonErrors.correction: Call the new numbers and allocate roles immediately.

commonErrors.error: Entering players wait for instructions.
commonErrors.correction: Scan the play and take the most valuable available role.

commonErrors.error: Players leave through the middle of play.
commonErrors.correction: Exit through the nearest interchange gate.

commonErrors.error: Teams do not adjust after turnover.
commonErrors.correction: Recount numbers and reorganise immediately.

progressions: Increase the frequency of number changes.
Remove visible number cards and use verbal calls only.
Add positional restrictions for entering players.
regressions: Limit changes to three-versus-two and three-versus-three.
Pause briefly after a number change.
matchApplication: Player numbers around the football change constantly as teammates and opponents arrive, leave or become involved elsewhere. Elite teams recognise these changes and reorganise faster than the opposition.

title: Advanced Ground-Ball Decision Assessment
primarySkill: Assessing advanced ground-ball decision making under deception, changing pressure, numerical imbalance and tactical risk
objective: Assess whether players can secure ground-ball possession and apply the correct tactical response when exits, numbers, pressure and support change unpredictably.
groundSize: Five assessment stations across approximately half an oval, plus one dynamic game area.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Establish five assessment stations:
Station 1: Deceptive pickup and defender manipulation.
Station 2: Late-closing outlet decision.
Station 3: One-versus-two survival.
Station 4: Exit risk matrix.
Station 5: Tempo control after possession.
Finish with the dynamic numbers ground-ball game.
Assign trained observers to every station.
Standardise starting positions, feeds and contact restrictions.
Give each player one familiarisation repetition.
Record decision quality and skill execution separately.
Manage fatigue so later stations remain valid.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players rotate through the five structured stations.
Each player completes three scored repetitions per station.
Coaches do not provide technical feedback during scored repetitions.
The player must respond to the live defensive and support picture.
Each repetition ends with a controlled exit, retention, turnover or neutral result.
Observers score scanning, collection, decision, execution and transition.
After the stations, teams complete two timed blocks of dynamic-numbers play.
Individual and team decisions are recorded during the game.
Results are reviewed after the full assessment.
Scores are used to identify technical, tactical and role-specific development needs.
coachingPoints: Standardise pressure while allowing genuine decisions.
Assess scanning before possession.
Separate collection quality from tactical choice.
Record whether the player updates the decision when information changes.
Reward retention or neutralisation when aggressive exit is unrealistic.
Assess tempo selection.
Evaluate risk against likely reward.
Record transition reaction after possession changes.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Pre-collection scanning.
Technical quality of the ground-ball win.
Ball protection under pressure.
Recognition of late outlet closure.
Decision making when outnumbered.
Use of deception.
Selection of corridor, wide or retention exits.
Tempo control after possession.
Communication with support.
Transition response after turnover.

commonErrors.error: Observers score only whether possession is retained.
commonErrors.correction: Assess scanning, decision quality and execution separately.

commonErrors.error: Defender behaviour varies significantly between players.
commonErrors.correction: Standardise defender starting rules and pressure limits.

commonErrors.error: Safe neutral decisions are scored as failures.
commonErrors.correction: Reward correct risk management in outnumbered situations.

commonErrors.error: Players receive coaching during scored repetitions.
commonErrors.correction: Provide feedback only after the station or assessment.

commonErrors.error: Later scores are reduced by unmanaged fatigue.
commonErrors.correction: Balance station order and schedule recovery.

commonErrors.error: A successful outcome hides a poor decision.
commonErrors.correction: Score process and result as separate criteria.

commonErrors.error: Written observations are too general.
commonErrors.correction: Record the exact cue missed, decision made and execution outcome.

progressions: Remove marked gates and visual cues.
Compare results across multiple training blocks.
regressions: Assess decision components separately before combining them.
matchApplication: Advanced ground-ball performance requires more than winning possession. Players must process changing pressure, support, numbers and field risk while maintaining technical control. This assessment measures whether those decisions remain effective under realistic complexity.
relatedDrills: GB-081 – Deceptive Pickup and False Exit

title: Successive Ground-Ball Possession Chain
primarySkill: Retaining team possession through successive ground-ball contests
objective: Develop the ability to win an initial ground ball, maintain support around the football and retain possession when the next disposal creates another loose-ball contest.
groundSize: Area approximately forty metres long and twenty-five metres wide with four staggered contest zones.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Mark four staggered ground-ball zones across the playing area.
Position three attackers and two defenders at the first zone.
Place one football or feeder at each subsequent zone.
The next football becomes active after possession exits the previous zone.
Attackers must rotate contest and support roles between zones.
Defenders recover and apply pressure at each new contest.
Mark a scoring gate beyond the fourth zone.
Teams change attacking and defending roles after each sequence.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach releases the first football into the opening contest.
One attacker enters while teammates provide outside support.
The attacking team attempts to extract possession.
Once possession exits the zone, the coach activates the next football.
Players release the previous football and transition towards the new contest.
The nearest attacker becomes the primary ground-ball player.
Other attackers reorganise outside and behind the football.
Defenders recover to contest possession and close outlets.
The sequence continues through all four zones.
The attacking team scores by retaining possession through the final gate.
coachingPoints: Treat every new football as a separate contest.
Allocate one primary ball winner at each zone.
Previous ball winners should rotate outside after disposal.
Support players must move before possession is established.
Maintain width and stagger between support options.
Secure each football before attempting the next connection.
React immediately when possession spills or changes.
Preserve one player behind the football where possible.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players identify the next active contest.
Whether one attacker assumes the inside role.
Whether previous ball winners rotate outside.
Whether support width is maintained.
Whether defenders recover effectively.
Whether each collection remains technically sound.
Whether the first disposal escapes local pressure.
Whether the team retains possession through all zones.

commonErrors.error: All attackers run directly to the next football.
commonErrors.correction: Nominate one inside player and preserve outside support.

commonErrors.error: The previous ball winner remains in congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Rotate outside immediately after disposal.

commonErrors.error: Players mentally relax after winning one contest.
commonErrors.correction: Re-focus instantly on the next active football.

commonErrors.error: Support options become level.
commonErrors.correction: Stagger depth around each contest.

commonErrors.error: The first disposal is rushed.
commonErrors.correction: Secure possession and release beyond pressure.

commonErrors.error: Defenders stop after losing the previous contest.
commonErrors.correction: Recover immediately and organise at the next zone.

progressions: Reduce the time between contest activations.
successIndicators: Win or retain each ground ball.
Preserve possession through the final gate.
matchApplication: Teams are often required to win several loose footballs within one possession phase. Sustained success depends on players repeatedly reorganising around the next contest rather than assuming one clean win has completed the play.

title: Ground-Ball Win to Immediate Defensive Press
primarySkill: Applying immediate team pressure when a ground-ball possession is lost after the initial win
objective: Develop the ability to transition instantly from attacking possession into a coordinated defensive press when the football is lost after a ground-ball win.
groundSize: Rectangle approximately thirty-five metres long and twenty-five metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into two teams.
Mark a central ground-ball contest zone.
Create a narrow corridor lane through the middle.
Place a scoring zone at each end.
Begin with three players from each team around the contest.
Position one additional support player from each team outside.
The coach starts every phase with a moving ground ball.
Controlled tackling is permitted.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach introduces the football into the central contest.
Teams compete for possession.
The team winning the ground ball attacks its scoring end.
After one or two disposals, the coach may call “turnover” and nominate the opposition to receive possession.
The team losing possession must apply immediate pressure.
The nearest player pressures the ball carrier.
Teammates protect the corridor and close short outlets.
If the pressing team regains possession, it counterattacks immediately.
A score is recorded when a team carries or disposes into the end zone.
Play resets with another ground-ball start.
coachingPoints: The nearest player applies pressure immediately.
The second defender protects the most dangerous central option.
Remaining players close short support and delay forward movement.
Avoid all defenders chasing the ball carrier.
Players behind the football must communicate the press shape.
The original ground-ball winner remains involved after disposal.
On regain, spread quickly into attack.
Maintain legal tackling technique during rapid transition.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players react immediately to possession loss.
Whether the nearest defender pressures the carrier.
Whether teammates protect central space.
Whether short outlets are closed.
Whether defenders avoid crowding the same opponent.
Whether tackling remains controlled.
Whether the team regains ground-ball possession.
Whether attacking shape returns quickly after regain.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after their team loses possession.
commonErrors.correction: Apply immediate pressure before the opponent can spread.

commonErrors.error: Every defender chases the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Allocate pressure, corridor and outlet roles.

commonErrors.error: The corridor remains unprotected.
commonErrors.correction: The second defender moves centrally first.

commonErrors.error: Players attempt low-percentage tackles from poor angles.
commonErrors.correction: Close space under control and tackle only when balanced.

commonErrors.error: The pressing team remains compressed after regaining possession.
commonErrors.correction: Spread immediately and create outside support.

commonErrors.error: Communication begins too late.
commonErrors.correction: Call defensive roles as soon as possession changes.

title: Corridor-Trap Ground-Ball Escape

Mark a narrow central ground-ball zone.
Position two attackers and two defenders around the football.
Place a third defender beyond the zone to bait and close the direct corridor exit.

The ball winner scans the apparent corridor exit.

The attacking team transfers possession beyond the trap.
Wide receivers continue forward through the scoring gate.
If defenders win possession, they attack a short counterattack gate.
Teams change roles after a set number of repetitions.

Secure the football before testing the exit.

Avoid slow lateral handballs that remain inside the trap.
Once the trap is escaped, accelerate forward.
Maintain one player underneath possession.

Whether the ball winner recognises the trap.
Whether possession is secured before release.
Whether wide receivers maintain spacing.
Whether rear support remains available.
Whether deception shifts the high defender.
Whether the first disposal escapes the central zone.
Whether the attacking team accelerates after the release.
Whether defenders coordinate the trap safely.

commonErrors.error: The ball winner attacks the corridor without reading the high defender.
commonErrors.correction: Scan beyond the immediate contest before committing.

commonErrors.error: Wide receivers collapse into the trap.
commonErrors.correction: Hold width and preserve the escape lanes.

commonErrors.error: Rear support stands too close.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain enough depth to receive with time.

commonErrors.error: The first handball travels sideways inside congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Release beyond the trap line.

commonErrors.error: Players escape but fail to accelerate.
commonErrors.correction: Attack the space immediately after clearing pressure.

commonErrors.error: Defenders close from unsafe angles.
commonErrors.correction: Approach under control and maintain legal contact.

title: Scoreboard-State Ground-Ball Decision Game
primarySkill: Adjusting ground-ball decisions according to score, time and match context

groundSize: Half an oval or rectangle approximately sixty metres long and forty metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into two teams.
Mark a scoring zone at each end.
The coach begins each phase with a ground ball.
Before the restart, announce the score margin and time remaining.
Use scenarios such as:
Scores level with sixty seconds remaining.
Attacking team six points behind with forty-five seconds remaining.
Possession team four points ahead with ninety seconds remaining.
Team requires percentage and must attack.
Controlled tackling is permitted.
Reset the scoreboard state after each phase.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach announces the scenario.
A ground ball is introduced into a contested area.
Teams compete for possession.
The ball winner must apply the tactical requirement immediately.
A trailing team attacks territory and scoring opportunities.
A leading team may retain possession, use width and avoid unnecessary risk.
Defenders respond to the likely tactical intention.
The countdown continues until a score, turnover, boundary exit or time expiry.
Teams briefly explain their decision after the phase.
A new scenario begins from a different field location.
coachingPoints: Know the score and time before entering the contest.
The same field picture may require a different decision under a different scenario.
Trailing teams should attack useful territory without becoming reckless.
Leading teams should retain possession without becoming passive.
Support players must understand the collective tactical requirement.
Protect central space after turnover.
Communicate time remaining.
Judge decisions by context, not only outcome.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players remember the score and time.
Whether the ground-ball winner adjusts the first action.
Whether support players reflect the tactical requirement.
Whether a trailing team gains territory.
Whether a leading team protects possession.
Whether defenders anticipate likely exits.
Whether players communicate time.
Whether turnover reaction matches the scenario.

commonErrors.error: Players ignore the announced score and time.
commonErrors.correction: Require the team to repeat the scenario before play begins.

commonErrors.error: A trailing team uses slow, low-risk possession.
commonErrors.correction: Attack territory and scoring opportunities with controlled urgency.

commonErrors.error: A leading team forces a corridor disposal.

The collector begins the approach.
The coach removes one support option using the colour card.
The nominated player exits the phase.

Players reset with a different support player removed.

Replace missing width, depth or rear cover immediately.

Mark a central ground-ball zone.
Position four attacking receivers around the outside.
Place one attacker as the initial collector.
Position three defenders at different numbered gates.

The nominated defender closes the next receiver.

The coach rolls the football to the central collector.
The player gathers and releases to an outside receiver.
The coach calls the first pressure number.
The nominated defender closes the receiver.
Other attackers reposition to provide new options.
The receiver protects possession and disposes away from pressure.
A different defender is called after the next disposal.

Players rotate collector, receiver and defender roles.

Recognise which pressure player has become active.
Move support away from the closing defender.
The receiver should protect possession before disposing.
Avoid returning the football towards the pressure source.

Whether the active defender is identified.
Whether support players adjust promptly.
Whether the receiver protects the football.
Whether disposal moves away from pressure.
Whether the chain maintains spacing.

Whether defenders rotate safely and realistically.

title: Chaos Ground Ball to Controlled Possession

coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into two teams.
Mark a central chaos zone approximately twelve metres × twelve metres.
Position two outside support players from each team beyond the zone.
The coach begins with a rolling, bouncing or deflected football.
During the opening phase, players may not dispose outside the chaos zone until their team establishes clean possession.
Once controlled possession is called, the team may exit through any gate.
The opposition transitions to defensive pressure.
Restart after a score, turnover or prolonged stoppage.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach introduces an unpredictable football into the chaos zone.
Players compete through spills, taps and second efforts.
Clean possession must be demonstrated before the team exits.
The ball winner protects possession and communicates control.
Outside support players establish width.
The first disposal moves beyond the chaos zone.
The possession team changes tempo and attacks a scoring end.
The defending team presses and protects central space.
If possession spills again, players reorganise around the new contest.
Play continues until a score, turnover or coach reset.
coachingPoints: Do not treat every touch as controlled possession.
Prioritise clean collection when available.
Use purposeful taps only when possession is unavailable.
Communicate clearly when the football is secured.
Outside players should hold width during the chaotic phase.
Change tempo immediately once control is established.
The first disposal must escape the chaos zone.
Reorganise instantly if possession breaks down again.

Whether second efforts continue.
Whether outside support remains available.
Whether ball winners communicate control.
Whether the first disposal exits congestion.
Whether tempo changes after control.
Whether teams reorganise after another spill.

commonErrors.correction: Secure possession before leaving the chaos zone.

commonErrors.error: Every player enters the central area.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain outside support on both sides.

commonErrors.correction: Direct touches to a teammate or recoverable space.

commonErrors.correction: Accelerate immediately before defenders reset.

commonErrors.correction: Hold width until possession is established.

Remove the requirement for a coach to call controlled possession.
Continue play across a larger area.

Stop after the first successful extraction.
successIndicators: Move the first disposal beyond congestion.
matchApplication: Many match phases contain several deflections and incomplete possessions before one team gains control. Elite teams recognise the exact moment control is established and change from contest mode into structured transition.

title: Intercept-Risk Ground-Ball Transition

Mark a central ground-ball contest zone.

Defenders score for intercepting or forcing a turnover.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach introduces the football into the central contest.
The collector secures possession under controlled pressure.

Do not assume a long kick is the fastest effective transition.

Whether intercept defenders influence the decision.
Whether handball is used to improve the angle.
Whether carrying is selected appropriately.
Whether kicks avoid protected space.
Whether targets move to create advantage.
Whether the final disposal is balanced.
Whether defenders transition after a turnover.
